Uniform Title: Parameśvarīmatatantra Manuscript: NGMPP Manuscript 5-5148, Reel No. B 133/3 Notes: Transcribed by the staff of Muktabodha under the supervision of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski from NGMPP reel no. B 133/3, manuscript no. 5-5148.
Revision 0: September 18, 2010. Chapters 15 to the end added. Publication country: India. Oṃ namaḥ śrīmahābhairavāya.
The Śrī Devī said: "O Lord, I have heard everything; it has been understood through your grace.
Now I wish to hear that which has come down through the lineage of succession."
How did Mount Meru arise, and what was its extraction like?
O Lord, what is the nature of the lineage in which the moving and unmoving world was born?
And the sixfold lineage tradition, joined with the sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa),
along with mantras, mudrās, and vidyās, which possess manifold forms and wonders.
In what manner and by what means is Vāgīśvarī, Mahāmāyā, Cāmuṇḍā, and Kulanāyikā established in the center of Meru?
Mṛtyuñjayā, Mahākālī, Troṭalā, Tripurabhairavī, Samayavidyā, the one known as Kulākārā, Siddhā, and Mārtaṇḍabhairavī.
O Mahādeva, she who is eternally great in deluding, the end-maker, and the supreme bestower of liberation—
the Mother of the Kula— is established in sixfold forms.
By whose grace Brahmā himself creates this world of the moving and the unmoving;
she is the power of Māyā, supremely secret, by which Janārdana is perfected.
She creates a net of illusion and many forms;
she is named Haṃsavāgeśvarī, who is produced from the remainder.
Sarasvatī is the great lore which was bestowed upon the six-faced one;
she is both the destroyer of desires and, furthermore, the one who provokes his anger.
Her arrows and bow indeed delude all that is moving and stationary;
by the grace of this Vidyā, Makaradhvaja attained perfection.
The Vakraprastārikā-vidyā, likewise the Brahmanityā-vidyā,
and the great Saṃjīvanī-vidyā by which Time (Kāla) has been brought under control.
Furthermore, O God, the womb-sacrifice is the cause for the birth of a son;
moreover, the vidyā that transfers poison is the destroyer of it.
O Lord of the Gods, this third procedure is called the "Cow of Plenty of Knowledge" (Vidyākāmadughā), which accomplishes the seven netherworlds and pertains to maidens.
How did the world of moving and non-moving beings arise from the gods in the center of Meru? O Bhairava, please grant us grace by explaining all of this in brief.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, to the supreme secret, the most excellent source of Meru,
by seeing which according to the prescribed method, one is liberated from all sins.
Whatever evil has been accumulated through action, mind, or speech—
all that comes to an end upon beholding the supremely auspicious Mount Meru.
That is the source of all sciences, especially of the Kaula;
from it arose the lineage and the sixfold Kulakrama.
They say that the family (kula) is the body, established in the form of power (śakti);
furthermore, knowledge in the form of space is declared to be Kaula.
Therein, in the center, the supreme and most difficult to attain realization has arisen;
the previously mentioned Kubjikāmata consists of nine crores [of verses].
In the midst of that, eighty-four thousand were extracted by me;
furthermore, right there in the center, the supreme Meru was extracted.
The divine sequence of transmission is established there in the center;
the extraction of all vidyās has arisen from that very center.
The mantras established in various treatises have been extracted in many ways;
yet all of them, being devoid of efficacy, are proclaimed to bring about obstacles along with their attendants.
O lady of excellent hips, those who abide outside of Meru do not attain success.
*Makāla-māye* is the letter *ra*, which is fire; *uviṣṇu* is the sky, [which is] flowing.
O Goddess, because Meru is the place of union through the obstruction [of the senses],
the Vidyā is extracted from the center of Meru, and the Krama is extracted from the center of Meru.
Through the grace of the Great Guru, one succeeds; there is no doubt in this.
There is no need for initiation, nor lineage, nor conduct, nor the knowledge arising from the Kaula tradition.
As long as one does not behold Meru, both command and authority remain;
until then, one wanders perpetually in saṃsāra like one with impaired senses.
O Goddess, for that sinner there is no such destination as that of a beast;
when Meru is seen, initiation is attained, and when Meru is seen, the destruction of impurity occurs.
Upon seeing me, one attains supreme peace without delay;
therefore, O lady of excellent complexion, I should be beheld with every effort.
One shall achieve the power of command and certainly obtain whatever one desires;
in a place that is auspicious, delightful, and where a great tree has been uprooted—
Combined with the expansion of the Vidyā-mantra, it originated from eighty-five cities;
there were gods, dānavas, siddhas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and kinnaras.
O lady of excellent complexion, all those stationed in the intermediate space behold [the Lord] and offer salutations by reason of their stainless purity.
Having beheld the supreme and auspicious Meru, they are liberated from all sins;
such a person is a fully accomplished family preceptor who awakens others to the meaning of this scripture.

One whose self is disciplined by the prescribed method, possessing complete and certain understanding (or: one who is complete and possesses firm resolve; or: one whose intellect is full and certain, in due order), should perform [the rite];
it must not be performed without the prescribed method, even if one were Maheśvara himself.
Therefore, with every effort, one should perform the auspicious and beautiful rite,
provided with the fivefold offerings and accompanied by perfumes and flowers.
Having smeared Mount Meru with camphor and saffron,
one should raise it up upon a ground altar, on a cloth, or on a beautiful mountain.
The wise one should draw lines and the worlds upon the chalk,
from east to west and from north to south.
There are one hundred and sixty-nine variously arranged compartments;
excluding the garland of the navel, those with faces in the caves begin from the eighth.
Placing the prince at the forefront, those which are doubled and aged,
broken on the left and right, should be arranged according to the sequence of the upper portions.
The number [of lines] for the directions is two, four, five, and twelve, excluding the eyes (two), the Vedas (four), and the seasons (six);
likewise, those that are broken at the bottom are of six types, as before.
O Great Goddess, when [the world] is shattered, shattered—those who abide there I shall tell you:
Kaivalya, the elements of the worlds, and likewise the nine classes of sages.
From this point forward, listen to [the sequence] joined with the eleventh [digit], according to the order of the upper portion (ūrdhvabhāga):
Viṣṇu, Rudra, Guha, the Mothers, and the various Bhairavas.
There is one named Meru, from which everything should be extracted;
Kailāsa is in the eastern part, while Gandhamādana is in the south.
Mandara is situated in the west, and Niṣadha is the abode in the north;
Mahāmeru has four peaks and is the accomplisher of all desires and goals.
Therein, one should construct the supreme Prastāra, the abode of all vidyās;
one should write the sixteen vowels beginning with 'a' and ending with the visarga.
There are thirty-four syllables adorned with five vowels;
the first is devoid of a vowel, while the second is joined with a vowel.
For each individual phoneme, however, two varieties are proclaimed (two are cited):
the first is uncombined with what precedes it, and the second is combined with the following one.
One should join the third with the half of the sixth, the fourth with the fourth, and the fifth with the fifth; thus one should extract [the mantra] beginning with the syllable Oṃ.
One should place [the syllable] preceded by the eastern letter at the end of *dhruva* and *nābhi*;
at the end of that, the peak of fragrance (*gandhaśikhara*); and the third at the end of *mandara*.
Furthermore, O Goddess, at the northern end, the letters of the Vedas are established;
[the letters] beginning with *dhruva* and ending with *dhruva* (or beginning with *dhruva* and having *dhruva* in the middle and at the end), as well as the elements and the flavors.
Among the vowels, the neuter ones are situated within the Vedas;
furthermore, among those [consonants], starting from the beginning and ending with the last, they are arranged from the east to the north.
O Ocean of Vowels, those vowels are situated in sequence by the number of the Vasus (eight).
There on Kailāsa, O fair-faced one, four worlds are located below the vowel *ṛ* (on Kailāsa, however, O fair-faced one, four worlds are below the two vowels *ṛ* and *ṝ*).
The beloved ones and others are situated there, established by numbers both numbered and unnumbered (the number of the Vedas).
The three situated in the middle of the sequence are located on Gandhamādana;
on Mandara, however, the four Vedic syllables are established above, namely *ṛ*, *ḷ*, *u*, and *ū*.
The three located in the middle of the *bhrū* [are those] which are in the north, in the abode of Niṣadha;
in the sky, on Mandara, O Goddess, and on Kailāsa, O Bhairavānanā.
The four letters beginning with *ka* are situated at the beginning and at both ends [of the alphabet];
likewise, three letters beginning with *kṣa* are situated at its end.
At the beginning, there are four syllables; at the end, in the houses of the Vedas;
at the conclusion, they are known as the Yugas; and likewise in the middle of Guḍa (Ogu).
The four elements are situated within the human body on the left and right sides;
having left the space between the sages (the central channel), they remain within the sheaths.
Within those [petals], arranged to the right and left, the Vasus are proclaimed, O Goddess, as nine in number, established according to their respective tastes and colors.
In the *Chā* and other [treatises], the Vedas are fully enumerated, as well as the other four;
among those, there are four varṇas (and others), which constitute the supreme *prastāra* established [by tradition].
This is the supreme, secret source (yoni), established as the emanation of mantra;
it is the source situated in the center, extending as far as the fourteen corners.
This Meru, with its four peaks and the abode of the gods, follows this sequence. Herein, various Siddhas and Vidyās have arisen;
they are obtained through the lineage of succession from the mouth of the Guru alone.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, the extraction of the Meru from the eighty-four thousand [verses], according to the Pārameśvarīmata within the Navakoṭi-saṃhitā.
The Goddess said:
Today my birth has become fruitful; today my ascetic penance has become fruitful, for I have heard the supreme secret concerning Meru, which causes the destruction of all sins.
And since you, O Lord of the Gods (O Śaṅkara, by whom I am gratified), have been pleased with me, I have attained purity;
now I desire to hear the names of those [deities] known as the Vidyās.
"How are they accomplished, O Lord of Gods, and what kind of power would there be?
Śrī Bhairava said: "First, there is the initiation and consecration which destroys all sins."
Thereafter, having understood the sequence of the goddesses (*devikrama*) as conjoined with the sixfold deposition (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*),
one should apply the Assembly of Sounds (*śabdarāśi*) known by the syllable *ku* to the limbs and faces [of the deity]. (The Assembly of Sounds, known by the syllable *ku*,
is conjoined to the limbs and faces.)
Then, by means of the sequential yoga, [he attains] Navātman and the rest, the supreme [Vidyā],
the three supreme secret Vidyās, and also the Aghorāṣṭaka.
Furthermore, there is another twelve-limbed [recitation], and then again one with six limbs;
thereafter, the placement (nyāsa) of the text and so forth, along with its grasping through three divisions.
There are twelve verses (or ten verses, as some say), as well as the Five Jewels;
the divine Fourfold Seat, conjoined with the Sixfold Placement.
Those who are disciplined in the Kula tradition consider the lineages of succession belonging to one consecrated by the Kula initiation to be the elders of the Krama.
This knowledge should be imparted to him who has endured the sequential placement (nyāsa);
one whose self is disciplined by the ritual rules should perform the placement three times a day, both by day and by night.
Whatever multitudes of sins exist throughout seven future births,
it burns them away by its mere placement, just as the sun does at the end of a kalpa.
In battles crowded with a multitude of weapons and at all stages of conflict, no fear exists for him; he is like a vajra-enclosure.
One should not engage in contact, eating, or conversation with anyone who is possessed of lust, anger, greed, deceit, or egoism.
One should never offer salutation even to an elder;
one should not fall at the feet of even a guru, for one will die—of this there is no doubt.
Therefore, one should avoid prostration with every effort;
I shall now describe the power attained through the practice of yoga for six months.
The fourfold collection of elements within wood, stone,
and minerals goes to destruction through prostration, just as a mountain struck by a vajra.
"O Goddess, in sixteen years, the state of moving through the sky (khecaratva) will be attained. The Goddess said: "O Lord, I do not even know what the sixfold deposition (ṣoḍhānyāsa) is like."
"O Lord of Gods, O Master, if you are pleased with me, you ought to speak.
Śrī Bhairava said: "O Goddess, as for that great mountain with four peaks which was described by me,"
I shall now fully explain the extraction of all vidyās as it stands in their midst,
and exactly how that extraction is to be performed.
O Goddess, on the peak of Kailāsa, one should know that Śrīkaṇṭha—the six-syllabled mantra, complete with its phonemes—is situated at the head; he is the deity there.
Furthermore, at the very end of that same Mount Gandhamādana,
on its peak, one should know that Ananta is situated within the circle of faces.
And the third Bhairava is situated there at the end of Mandara;
Trimūrti is located in the middle of the right eye and resides in the left eye.
His house, extending to Niṣadha, originated from the letters of the Vedas; it was established facing Amarārīśa, beginning with Dhruva and situated within the letters of the elements.
Having placed Arghīśa, who possesses the color of the seasons, upon the right ear,
the placement on the left ear brings about the destruction of all sins.
On Kailāsa, in the middle of the left side, situated below Śrīkaṇṭha,
one should place Bhairava Bhārabhūti upon the nostril of Bhānu.
That guest is in the middle, while the eighth is on Gandhamādana;
those ending in the anusvāra and visarga reside in Loka, and on Mandara and Vidura.
One should recognize Sthāṇu-Rudra and place him on the right cheek;
he dwells in the midst of Niṣadeka and is the great destroyer of the name of Rudra.

O lady of excellent complexion, the placement [of mantras] should be performed on the surface of the left cheek; Kailāsa is located at the beginning of the throat, extending to the ear by its respective name.
The wise one should place Bhūtīśa in the row of teeth, in the middle of the fangs;
one should extract his seed-syllable with "ru" at the end and at the beginning as well.
One should know that Sadyojāta, who is established as multicolored, first resides in the left nostril; he is to be placed in the middle of the lip (and on the head).
Rudra is the Lord of Grace, possessed of great splendor and a noble mind;
therefore, with every effort, one should place the letter *ḷ* at the end of the lower [lip].
One should know Aṅkūra at the tip of the uvula, Visargaja at the root of the tongue,
Mahāsena, and the exceedingly powerful Rudra as well.
Having carefully performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Great Rudra named Krodha, originating from the left cheek and so forth up to the base of the right arm.

Furthermore, O Sovereign of the Gods, having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) right there in the middle of the arms upon the Lord named Caṃśu, who stands in the midst of space; p. 4b) thus it is done.

One should know the letter *pa* as the western limit; one should place the elbows below in the letter *kha*. They say that the letter *gha*, preceded by its phonetic class, is Śiva in the *kaṅkāla* (or *kaṅkaṇa*).
Placing one foot upon the hand, it is situated at the end of Arghīśa;
the tortoise [syllable] is situated in the middle of the letter *ca*, resting at the base of the left [hand].
One should first place the syllable *va* situated on the left arm, as if resting on a single hand;
then one should place the syllable *ja*, joined with four faces, situated at the elbow.
The syllable *rū* is placed upon the bracelet; the unconquered one (*Ajitā*) is the deity there.
She who has arisen from the syllable *svā* (or *yānta*) is established on the right hand, bestowing peace through the arising of the nine syllables.
Thus, O Great Goddess, the placement is established on both arms;
at the base of the shank is the half-moon, and there they know Soma-īśvara to reside.
One should know that to the south is the Full Moon, adorned by the thighs (and situated upon the lunar form);
there, O Great Goddess, one should station Lāṅgalīśa.
Having first performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) with the *ātmapūjā*, one should place Dāruka between the knees;
he was previously situated within the garland of planets and is now established in the middle of the shanks.
Having diligently performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Lord Ardhanārīśvara,
one should place Umākānta, situated in the middle of the letter *ṇa*, upon the right foot.
The letter *takāra* is at the root of the left [hand], known by the name Āṣāḍhī;
the nyāsa performed in that location is the second, situated below.
O Goddess of the Gods, having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon Daṇḍin situated in the center of Meru,
the letter *ḍha* is above it and the letter *cha* (or *hi*) is situated below.
One should know the placement at the knees by the name Dhātrīśa;
one should apply the letter *ja*, situated between *da* and *dha* (i.e., *ja*), in the place of the shanks.
At the end of Dhruva, situated above the position of the letter *ta*,
the great Rudra named Meṣa is established on the left foot.
O lady of excellent complexion, one should place the blood located in the right side of the belly;
the syllable *tha* (or *ṭha*) is situated upon whose head, and below it is the syllable *ṣa* (and gold is its precursor).
One should place Bhūtādi, who resides on Mount Mandara, in the left side of the belly;
and one should establish Śikhivāhimahārudra stationed in that very place.
One should recognize that for whom the syllable *mo* is situated above, in the middle of the back, there is the "goat-testicle" (*chagalaṇḍa*); Rudra is established therein.
On Mount Mandara, situated below the Ṛṣimālā ridge, one should know that the navel-center is located there; the deity Viraṇḍa resides therein.
In that very same *Ṛṣimālā*, one should know that Mahākāla is situated in the center of the letter *bha*; he is situated in the center of the heart.
In the central square marked with the syllable Ya, to the east of which the letter Go is situated, there is Vāgīśa Bhairava; he is the most excellent among the supreme [deities] of the skin.
At its end is Rakta-vaktra; in the center, however, within the group of nine, stands Bhūjaṅga-bhairava, who resides there upon the flesh of the wielder of the Pināka bow.
One should recognize this seed-syllable as being placed there for the wielder of the Pināka bow, wherein the letter *ri* is situated before the position below the letter *sa*.
O lady of excellent complexion, one should place the seed-syllable situated in the middle of the *vecā* and established in the middle of the sinew; there, one should install Khaḍgīśa Bhairava.
He whose ultimate refuge is established below the end of the Lord of Speech (vāgīśa)—
Rudra, who dwells within the marrow— [should be meditated upon] correctly by name after name.
If there is the letter *ra* below it, and the letter *ka* situated before it,
with that same letter located in the very middle, he is Bhairava by name.
One should know that when the Pinākin is situated below at the end of the Sivāra, it resides in Śukra; this is Bhairava by the name of Bhṛgu.
Khaḍgīśa Bhairava is situated above there;
they say Lakulīśa is the vital breath (prāṇa), situated below Arghīśa.
One should know that Rudra, who stands in the midst of Krodha and is situated at the end of the letters,
is Saṃvartaka, the bringer of destruction at the end of the Yuga.
This collection of sounds is proclaimed to be the destroyer of all sins;
it should be placed upon all parts of the body, enclosed within the five *praṇavas*.
On difficult paths, amidst water and fire, in the presence of fierce fanged beasts, and in times of fear;
in debate, in dispute, and in battle—nowhere does any fear exist.
Wherever the lord of practitioners may dwell,
by the contact with his rosary, he goes to the world of Rudra.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Śaka Rāśi," in the eighty-four thousand [verse] *Navakoṭisaṃhitā* according to the *Pārameśvara-mata*.
The Śrī Devī said:
"O Lord, O Bhairava, you have described the ritual placement (nyāsa) through the union with the five praṇavas;
I desire to hear that [further] by your grace."
The illustrious Bhairava said:

Listen, O Goddess, to the supreme secret, which is difficult to obtain—the extraction [of mantras], as well as the ritual placement (nyāsa), worship, and consecration; nothing should be performed without these.
I shall describe that deity of the five praṇavas,
whose syllable on Kailāsa was previously and originally neuter.
That which is situated in the temple, pervading the head of the quarters of the world,
is this primordial union with the *praṇava*, from which the mobile and immobile universe has arisen.
Having extracted the syllable *chā*, which is established upon the *la* and the *kuśala* [syllables],
O Goddess, his seat is established as being situated within the *nava*.
They know the second *praṇava* as that which is pierced at its head by the three forms (*trimūrti*), adorned with a *bindu* upon its crest, and produced from the Supreme Power (*paraśakti*).
That syllable which has Vāgīśa below and the Krodha-syllable above,
is mounted upon the letter Ra and joined with the fourth vowel.
The seed-syllable of cruel appearance, which bestows sovereignty, was formerly given on Mount Mandara; having then seized Śikhivāhana, [he departed].
Jhaṇṭīśa is placed on the head, seated upon a serpent-throne;
it is declared to be the fourth Praṇava, adorned with a Bindu at its crest.
This is the most terrible seed-syllable, which, by its mere recollection, causes the cosmic egg to be utterly destroyed, like the blazing fire at the end of time that has been unleashed.
The letter *ś* is the life-force (*prāṇa*) of the preceding vowel situated at the top;
Sāvitrī is placed upon the head, and its pronunciation includes the nasal dot (*bindu*).
The *praṇava* is said to be *nirvāṇa*, situated upon the seat of fire;
these five great seed-syllables are the primordial elements in the *Ākulāgama*.
The ritual placement (nyāsa), worship, and the consecration (saṃskāra) must not be devoid of this;
O Goddess, it has been taught as the supreme secret, encapsulated by the five praṇavas.
Always perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and worship according to this very method;
one should know that this is the sequential [practice], and one shall obtain the fruit of the four aims of life (*caturvarga*).
The Goddess said:
"O Goddess, [I shall give] the thirty-two-syllable mantra which accomplishes all desires and aims;
[it is worshipped by] Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva."
By means of these five deities, the lords of the gods attained perfection;
I desire to hear, according to the truth, about that which is the primordial, supreme, and subtle source.
In that very instant, the sins of many births and rebirths are reduced to ashes.
Śrī Bhairava said: In the beginning, the syllable was produced among the Rudras in the abode of the sages.
In the center of which, O Great Goddess, is the mighty Rudra Māyāmeṣa.
One should know that previously, Mālinī is situated on the head;
previously, the vowel of Vāgīśa is established above the *strāyu*.
The second arose from the navel, and Rudra is the third;
the color situated within the garland of planets is then established in the center.
O Supreme Goddess, the sinew is Rudra; at its tip is the fifth [letter],
Bhūtīśa, which is mounted upon Vāgīśa and Śānta and situated on the head.
In the sixth [syllable] one should recognize the seed-syllable; at its end is he who has the peacock as his vehicle (Skanda). Above that, on his head, is situated the seat of the letter Ra.
One should place Jhaṇṭīśa upon the head, situated above Kūranta;
this is the supreme heart-seed syllable (*hṛdbīja*), O Goddess, which bestows all accomplishments.
Having extracted the color of wrath (the letter *kṣa*), it stands upon the seat of Amarī;
the eighth seed-syllable (*ha*) should be placed before that letter *va*.
The subtle Rudra is placed on the head, with four faces situated below;
before him is the garland of Rudras, and Vāgīśa accompanied by Bhūti.
Mounted upon the red Laṅkuḷī, with the consonant situated at the head,
conjoined with Ananta and Ananta— this is the supreme twelfth seed-syllable.
Again, having raised the *prāṇa* twice in the two locations, O Maheśvarī,
one should cause both letters to be placed upon the *bhujaṅgama* seat for them.
O Trimūrti, it is not adorned by the consonant nor by the color;
Arghīśa and the seat are likewise there, and beyond that, the consonant above.
One should extract the letters ending with Krodha and Kūrma, as well as the consonants of the *ṭa* and *ta* groups,
and place them alone at the beginning of those ending in *e*.
Then again, there should be the syllable Śrīkaṇṭha alone,
followed by that which is joined with Sadyojāta, namely Śiveśa Parameśvara.
O Goddess of the gods, the seed-syllable that removes all sins is located in the twenty-first [chapter];
it is joined with the letter *na* and is situated in red at its end.
Furthermore, O Goddess, Mahākāla is situated on the seat of the right ear;
he is the second in the group of wrathful deities and is distinguished by his threefold form.
The twenty-fourth seed-syllable is the bestower of accomplishment;
it is situated within the vital breaths (prāṇa) and others, and the Tortoise (Kūrma) is positioned above it.
They know the twenty-fifth [letter] as being joined with the end of *krūra*;
again, that same [letter] is joined with *krūra* and adorned with the vowel of the Vedas (*vedasvara*).
O Great Goddess, at its forefront is the supreme abode of Krodharudra,
the twenty-seventh great [center], which is joined with Sukṣmarudra.
The syllable arising from the right foot is the abode of Umā’s consort;
it is the twenty-eighth seed-syllable, subtle, and situated above that.
One should sow the seed again; both [the letters] are established at the beginning.
Again, the phoneme situated in the sinew is conjoined with the subtle Rudra.
Joined with Jhaṇṭīśena, the Tortoise (Kūrma) is situated above it;
this is the supreme secret Vidyā, established as the power of Parāśakti.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
these indeed originate from the five faces, and they reside within these vidyā-faces.
The Grandfather of all beings was born from the eastern face,
and again, O Goddess, he was born from the northern face of Nārāyaṇa.
The eleven Rudras and those born from the mouth of Yama have attained perfection;
there is no doubt in this matter due to the power of this vidyā.
And Īśvara, O Great Goddess, is born from the eastern face;
Śiva, the perfected one, both transcendent and immanent, resides in the upper face, O Mistress of the Gods.
O Great Goddess, at every bend [of the path], these best of gods are indeed perfected;
even those who are not yet perfected become perfected when they have previously been joined with the perfected ones.
O Great Goddess, those devoted to the performance of ritual practice say "Gandharva" with their hearts;
they are intent upon worship and propitiation. (The Gandharvas say it with their heads; the Siddhas [say] "Gandharva" with their heads.)
And he attained the state of a Gandharva through the power of Śirodevī;
those great sages who dwell here are perfected through austerity, truth, and self-restraint.
The thirty-two syllables of the Goddess, who are devoted to the worship of Śiva,
are declared to be the Jñānasiddhas, inhabitants of the upper world.
All the deities beginning with Indra, Dharmarāja Yama, Nīla,
Nirṛti, Varuṇa, and those such as Yakṣas and Kubera;
O lady of excellent complexion, they are perfected in this armor; of this there is no doubt.
[The deities are] the Moon, the Sun, Guha, and then the signs beginning with Aries, Taurus, and so forth.
Through the practice of propitiating the Eye, they have all attained perfection; of this there is no doubt—neither the Nāgas, nor the Vidyādharas, nor any of the mountains, oceans, or rivers.
O Goddess of the gods, those beings who were born on earth, in the netherworld (pātāla), and from the source of weapons,
formerly attained their respective perfections through the practice [of this mantra].
O Goddess, O Sovereign of the Gods, by your grace, the thirty-two-syllable Vidyā exists within the world for whomever possesses its power.
The three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile, are produced from the womb of knowledge;
O Goddess, this is the supreme Māyā, established as the form of the creation of mantras.
O Goddess of gods, by worshipping [Him], the three worlds become worshipped;
O fair-faced one, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon His limbs and faces.
The Goddess said:
"O God, I have heard the supreme secret, the most excellent meditation on the extraction of the Goddess,
as well as her limbs and faces which were described by you."
"I desire to hear that from you through your grace, O Bhairava.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"I shall tell it to you without a doubt, that which has been asked by you."
What is the seven-syllable root mantra of the Goddess, and what would its form be at the end of each [syllable]?
I shall explain that to you without doubt;
it is mounted upon Khaṇḍapāvaka, with Khaṇḍamāyā situated below.
One should cause the vital breath (prāṇa) to ascend to the crown of the head; before that [breath] is Āṣāḍhī, and there is also Mahākāla alone, mounted upon a seat of the color of wrath.
Pinākin may become the color; then again, there is the solitary [syllable].
These are the Vedic syllables, and the seven sciences are situated at their end.

One should write the seven vidyās at its end; these four [syllables] one should draw at the end of that. At the end of that, one should write the heart-mantra; they know it to consist of ten and eight syllables.
The divine heart-mantra of Kubjikā, which accomplishes all desires,
consists of three syllables situated at the end of Rudra, which follow the root-vidyā.
The head consists of those twice-born [syllables] together with Ātma-Ārttaṇḍa and Bhairavī;
at the end of the world are the seed-syllables of the elements, while the Root-Vidyā is firmly established [therein].
The goddess named Jñānaśikhā is established with the ending *vauṣaṭ*;
the armor (*kavaca*) is proclaimed to consist of five syllables at the end of the crest-lock (*śikhā*).
The vajra of the Goddess, the destroyer of all [obstacles], is like a cage;
before it stand the Vedas and the Three-eyed One.
The goddess who beholds the three worlds has arisen as the four-syllabled mantra; at the end of the Vidyā are the letters of the pair, which abide within the three of the goddess.
The goddess Sarvārtharakṣaṇī is present in all the cardinal and intermediate directions;
she is joined with the mantras ending in *namaḥ*, *svāhā*, *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭ*, *huṃ*, and *phaṭ*.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully declare the faces of the Goddess,
beginning with the letter *na* and ending with the letter *ya*, which are the phonemes established within Rudra.
One should worship the power of emanation (sṛṣṭi-śakti), ending with "namaḥ," on the eastern face;
and at its conclusion, those of beautiful color are produced on the northern face.
The power of Māyā, ending with the word "namaḥ," should be worshipped with great effort;
furthermore, O Goddess, on the southern face, the letters of the elements are situated.
Through union with the power Raudrī, worship should be performed ending with "namaḥ. In the west are the seasonal colors, which bestow power and sovereignty.
By worshipping that which ends with *namaḥ*, one obtains the fruit of the power of will (*icchā-śakti*);
the two eyes situated in the upper syllables are declared to be the power of liberation (*mokṣa-śakti*).
One who worships according to the prescribed rite is liberated from all sins (and bonds).
Furthermore, whatever seed-syllables of the Vidyās reside within these five faces—
At the beginning, one should perform the utterance of whichever [mantra] has whatever kinds of five-faced limbs; this is the ritual placement (nyāsa) conjoined with the *praṇava*.
"O Goddess, one should recite the Root-Vidyā, which bestows all accomplishments.
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Extraction of the Limbs and Faces of the Five Praṇavas of the Root-Vidyā," according to the Pārameśvara-mata.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme Nyāsa of Navātman. Having extracted the syllable of the navel (Na), Prāṇa shall be its seat.
The vital breath (prāṇa) mounted upon blood, and blood seated upon the seat of wrath;
the wrathful one on the seat of Mahākāla, and Mahākāla, the wielder of the Pināka bow.
The wielder of the Pināka bow [should visualize] the syllable *snā* mounted upon the syllable *mā*, with the syllable *u* above the syllable *r*;
it is mounted upon all [the preceding syllables] up to the end of *dhruva* (the syllable *o*), and is adorned with *nāda* and *bindu*.
One should perform this placement (*nyāsa*) of the non-self upon all the limbs and the body [as follows]:
"Mahākāla, the wielder of the Pināka bow, mounted upon the sinews of Pinākī."
Mounted at the end of *dhruva* (the syllable *oṃ*), adorned with *nāda* and *bindu*,
one should diligently perform this placement (*nyāsa*) upon all the limbs of the body;
for him, no fear exists within the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile.
The illustrious Bhairava said: O Goddess, she who is the supreme secret, Mālinī, born from the Mātṛkā,
illuminates with her own splendor within the body all that is stained, both moving and unmoving.
Listen with one-pointed minds to its supreme secret extraction:
the great Rudra named Meṣa is established as the root of the Vidyā and so forth.

That syllable, of that same color, is placed upon the head; O Goddess, it is established as the Resounding One (nādinī). The syllable situated in the middle of the Lord (nātha) rests above the Red One (lohita).
Known as Grasani, she is situated within the circle of the face;
Bhārabhūti and Spatithi are likewise established at the tip of the nose.
These vowels on the right and left cheeks are neuter;
they correspond to Nivṛtti, Pratiṣṭhā, Vidya, and Śānti.
O Goddess, this garland of heads, Mālinī, is situated upon the head;
O Goddess, furthermore, the third [syllable], which has the color of a tortoise, is situated in the eye.
Having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa), Cāmuṇḍā, the destroyer of all obstacles,
is again [visualized] between the two eyes as the goddess of pleasing appearance.
One should install the color arising from Mīnarudra according to the prescribed rite;
furthermore, the goddess Nārāyaṇī is situated between the two ears.
One should first perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of that which resides in Umā’s ear:
the goddess Mohinī, beginning with the syllable *dhruva*, is the ornament upon the right ear.
The end of Dhruva is situated in the left ear for the sake of Prajñā;
Kaivalya is located on Mount Mandara and is established at the tip of the nose.
One should know the secret power (guhyaśakti) within the center of the vajra of the Vajrī; there resides the Lord Khaḍgī, situated at the end of the letter Va.
Karālī, Kapālī, Śivā, Aghorā, and Vaśīrvarā—
these five are established in the group of wrathful deities (krodhavarga) according to their sequential order.
O Goddess of the gods, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) from below to above upon the rows of teeth:
[the powers] Aṣṭavāgīśvarī, Vācā, Trimūrti, and Sarasvatī.
One should perform the deposition on the tongue, placing the syllable *va* in the middle of the throat;
there, situated in the center, is the goddess renowned as Śikhivāhinī (She Who Has the Peacock for a Vehicle).
Having been raised up by the sages of old, the formidable [Liṅga] is established there;
on its right arm, upon the staff, stands a peak adorned with a temple.
In that very place, situated in the middle watch of the night within the Ṛṣimālā,
Vāyuvegā is established at the peak of the left hand.
Homage to the goddess Vināyakī, who stands upon a seat of beautiful color on the staff-like right arm,
and who is established in the colors of the planets and other celestial bodies.
One should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the staff-like left arm starting from the middle of the full-moon hand,
and having performed the placement on the hands through the conjunction with the letters ending in *ḍha*.
And for the goddess Rūpikā, who is established in the description of Ajitā,
the placement of the fingers upon the right hand must be performed.
Furthermore, O Goddess Pārvatī, she performed the finger-assignment (aṅgulī-nyāsa) on her left hand;
through the union of all the phonemes, she became established at the end of space.
Dīpanī holds a trident-staff and a serpent in her right hand;
they say that Jayantī holds a trident, which is the first [mantra] of the letter Ja.
In her left hand she holds a skull-cup, and her color is that of the moon; she is seated upon the throne of Someśvara and is renowned among those called Kapālīs, established in her left hand.
O Goddess, Pavanī is indeed in the heart, preceded by the color red;
and Ambikā is situated therefrom in the middle of my mouth.

The placement (nyāsa) of the vital breath (prāṇa) must be performed; the power of will (icchā-śakti) resides in the heart. At the end of the world, the extraction of that syllable is situated as before.
One should place the letter *sa* joined with the nasal drop (*bindu*) in the center of the heart;
having performed this placement (*nyāsa*) with effort for the sake of the Supreme Self, one should [worship] the Goddess.
The complexion of the goat is the same as that of Ekahasta; Chāgalī is situated there, while they know Pūtanā to be located between the right breast and on the left.
There, having placed the syllable *pinākī* in the eastern half, one should install it;
through union with *ananta*, [it is located] in the midst of the milk of the *āmoṭī* plant.
Furthermore, the goddess Lambinī, together with her own [consort],
should diligently perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) situated within the center of the abdomen.
The goddess Saṃhārikā, situated in the center of Saṃvarttaka,
should be known as the placement (nyāsa) upon the navel, preceded by Mahākālī.
O Supreme Goddess, one should place the Nyāsa situated in the middle of the *nitamba*;
then, in the first syllable of the worlds, one should place the arrows of the Flower-Armed God (Kusumāyudha) upon the secret parts.
In the midst of Saṃvarka is the goddess Śukrā (Sūkṣmā), who is established there;
she is conjoined with the cruel Āṣāḍhī, and Tārā is likewise established therein.
The placement located in the middle of the thighs has been described; now hear about the placement on the knees.
Having extracted the syllables beginning with 'nā' (or 'vā'), one should place Jhaṇṭīśa wherever he resides.
One should place [the letter] ending in *ṛ* at the left knee with the effort of the power of knowledge (*jñāna-śakti*),
which is established on Kailāsa.
The power of action (kriyā-śakti) resides there; one should diligently perform the ritual placement (nyāsa).
The Gāyatrī of Sadyojāta is situated upon the right shanks.
Sāvitrī is on the left calf, with the letter *Ṛ* preceding it;
Dahanī is established upon the seat of the letter *Da* on the right foot.
One should diligently perform the placement (nyāsa) of the syllable *pha* (as *phetkāri*) on the left foot;
O Goddess, this supreme secret is the most excellent *mālinī* placement.
Arranged according to the rules of ritual procedure and encapsulated by the five *praṇavas*,
[it wards off] ghosts, spirits, and fiends, as well as yakṣas, rākṣasas, and great serpents.
Moreover, O woman of inferior birth, whatever other harmful beings are present there flee in the ten directions at the mere fall of his glance.
In the face of the falling of thunderbolts and lightning, and during fears of kings and thieves, one attains victory in battle; no wound from weapons shall be found.
He shall indeed possess great protection against all weapons;
he shall obtain incomparable good fortune, long life, and the perfection of health.
If one performs the ritual placement (nyāsa) with effort while staying in a cremation ground,
he will be seen blazing by bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas.

O beautiful one, if she has performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) seven times, she grants vast accomplishment (*siddhi*) through the practice at night, even when mounted upon an elephant or a horse.
Alternatively, having grasped a weapon in his hand with the *abhūmipāda* [step],
the great hero enters into battle with those who desire to fight.
In the case of an enemy army, however, they are seen in the form of a single mass;
O Goddess, that which consists of a body of fifty forms is seen as one.
Striking with a multitude of weapons while mounted upon elephants,
they will undoubtedly return after having conquered the enemy armies.
Such is the power of the application of the Mālinī-nyāsa:
in the end, one attains liberation, and there is no further rebirth.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter on the Mālinī-nyāsa in the Pārameśvara-mata.
The illustrious Bhairava said: O Goddess, I shall again proclaim the supreme secret in its proper sequence:
namely, the Parā, the Aparā, and likewise the Parāparā.
O Goddess of the gods, by performing the ritual placement (nyāsa), one is liberated from all sins;
indeed, the five praṇava-mantras reside in the primary locations.
Having joined [the syllables] beginning with *parā-vidyā*, one should then place Śrīkaṇṭha;
having first extracted Śiva, he should be conjoined with Sadyojāta.
Through union with the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti), they know the fifth to be the serpent (bhujaṅga);
it is situated above the letter 'dīpinī' (the letter *u*) and the end of 'prāṇa' (the letter *ha*), starting from the ninth.
One should draw [the deity] joined with the Trimūrti and endowed with the origin of the worlds;
furthermore, the goddess Ambikā is situated together with Śukrabhairava.
And the seventh great seed stands before one at the end of the world;
having extracted the purifying seed, that which is situated there is red.
Furthermore, O Goddess, one should again draw a serpent in front of the Navamantra,
and in front of that, one should again write the color originating from Mahākāla.
Joined with the portion of the syllable *Śivāya* and united with *Sadyojāta*,
it stands before the nine [vowels] through the yoga of *Ṛ* and the others.
One should place the seat beginning with *dhruva* and situated at the head beginning with *loka*;
it is positioned in the middle of these syllables, below the end of *dhruva*.
At the end of Dhruva and at the end of Anta, it is adorned with Sadyojāta;
this is called the fourteenth, and immediately after that is Dīpinī.
Furthermore, that supreme sixteenth seed-syllable, which resides on the staff of the trident and is situated upon the seat at the end of the *dhruva*, should again be placed before him.
Immediately following that, one should take the red [syllable] conjoined with Jhaṇṭīśena;
then, having extracted the seed-syllable Bhṛkhu?ka, which is situated upon the head of Ambikā.
One should write the letter at the end of the fortnight (pakṣānta) together with the visarga, placed upon the head;
having extracted the vowel ṛ and so forth, Śiva is established therein.
Immediately following this, the seed-syllable joined with Rudra and Anta,
conjoined with Ananta, is known as the twentieth [syllable] (the fifth serpent).
O Goddess, situated in my center is Mālinī, who stands upon the seat of Amarīśa;
she is the seed-syllable that is most difficult to attain.
O Bhairavānanā, O beloved, having taken *bhāradbhūti* below *pracaṇḍa*,
the thirty-second seed-syllable (*bīja*) is joined with the first vowel, which is most secret.
Having extracted the one preceded by the Ṛṣi (the letter *u*), joined with the tongue of Mālinī (*ī*),
and having taken the solitary *va* and *ca*, it is situated in the heart of Bhairava.
Furthermore, one should draw his beloved at the very beginning, standing before him;
having raised up Umākānta, he is endowed with the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti).

O Dear One, there Bhairava Chagalaṇḍa stands before that [deity], who is of the color of a goat; furthermore, Mahākāla is likewise situated in front of him. O Goddess, in the midst of the drinking [vessel] is the red [liquid], joined with the subtle.
And at its front is Rudra the sinew, with Mālinī situated in his mouth.
Furthermore, these seeds are situated at both ends (and four are situated at the beginning).
Having extracted both vital breaths (the syllables *ra* and *kṣa*), they are joined with *jhiṇṭiśena* and so forth.
And its very tip alone, O beautiful one, where Ambikā is situated,
should be raised up, being red in color, at the junctions of the yugas.

O Bhairavī, the two phonemes of consciousness (C and V), which were previously situated, remain established in their seats beginning with Dhruva; these two are situated before that, and they are indeed absolute.
One should again write the five *praṇavas* and so forth situated within it; furthermore, one should place the seed-syllable of the universe (*viśvabīja*) before that by means of the *vidyā*.
Having extracted the syllable beginning with *bhūta* (the letter *bha*), place it within the *Dīpinī* (the letter *i*).
That which is preceded by *ṛ* (*ṛ*) is given as the head; the wise know the heart of the Supreme (*para*) to be [the syllable] *parasya*.
Whatever was previously [stated] regarding this seed-syllable, do not enclose it;
and one should place the seed-syllable of this Vidyā (the Viśva-vidyā) before it.
This supreme knowledge, O Goddess, is difficult to obtain in the three worlds;
its four and forty seed-syllables are established as the very essence of life.
Half [of the first] and three syllables, and another [half] thereafter—listen [to this]; one should apply it at the end.
The second [syllable] begins with the *praṇava*, and the first is the supreme seed-syllable (*bīja*).
Mounted upon a serpent-throne, adorned by the letter *Ha* and others, with the head surmounted by the letter *Ṭha* at its beginning— this seed-syllable is most difficult to obtain.
Taking the letter *va* with its vowel above, adorned by the letter *va* [as a nasal],
the seed-syllable is the goddess Śukrā, crowned by the head [the letter *ha*], and worshipped by the best of gods.
Place the *prāṇa* (the letter *ha*) mounted on the end of *dhruva* (*o*), joined with the *bindu* (the nasal *m*) and the seed-syllable *ṇa*;
then again, [place] *mālinī* (the letter *i*) and the left foot (*la*) alone.
Mounted upon the Dhruva-maṇḍala and situated in front of the half-moon,
she is known as Aparā, the destroyer of all obstacles.
I shall now describe its door, which belongs to the Yakṣāparāparā Devī;
it is the direct bestower of all accomplishments and the granter of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
At the end of the syllable *dhruva* (oṃ), having grasped it below, one should write the letter *kṣānta* (kṣa) situated above it,
mounted upon the color white, together with the *visarga*.

Having again performed the placement beginning with the *praṇava*, O lady of excellent complexion, one should perform the placement of the name of the Vidyā— both the supreme and the non-supreme— upon all the limbs of the body.
One obtains dharma, kāma, artha, and mokṣa; of this there is no doubt.
Śrī Bhairava said:
I shall now proclaim the supreme eightfold great nyāsa (mahānyāsa) of Aghora.
Having extracted [the mantra] beginning with the Praṇava, Śrīkaṇṭha follows immediately after;
it is joined with the eighth vowel, which is unprecedented (or "without 'ma'"), and is situated on Gandhamādana.
The third is declared to be Śūladaṇḍa,
and the fourth is the supreme seed-syllable, which pierces the head of Apūrveśa.
At its end is the goddess Ambika, situated in the abode of the letter Cha;
she is joined with the Viśvamālā and others, resides in the letter Ra, and has a bindu upon her head.
And the fifth is the great seed-syllable, joined with the semen and the initial emission;
it is the placement on the head of Aghorī, established in the color of the seasons.
The first seed-syllable begins with the Praṇava; the second is the staff of the trident, joined with the seat of Amṛtā and adorned with a Bindu at its head.
Having extracted the letter *pā* and the pure third [letter],
and the fourth alone, O Goddess, which is the serpent, the abode of Bhairava.
In front of that, the syllable *mālinī* stands alone as the buttocks;
at its end (front), they say it is *śiva*, adorned with the ending of *rudra*.
One should draw the red-colored [deity] with Jhaṇṭīśa situated on his head;
having extracted the letter ending in *cha*, he is seated upon the throne of Amarīśa.
The goddess Śrī is proclaimed as the seventh, surmounted by the letter Ś;
one should cause the universal seed-syllable of Parā to be bestowed as the eighth.
The syllable of Bhṛgu joined with the visarga is placed before that;
these are the nine yogas conjoined with Paramaghora.
One should perform the placement on the curved parts (vakranyāsa), and after that, the placement on the throat (kaṇṭhanyāsa).
Having extracted the letter preceding 'ṛ' (i.e., 'i') and adorned it with the head-vowel (the bindu), [one places it there].
They say that before it is the letter "rakta" (ra), the second being established as the color;
then the letter preceded by "ṛ" joined with the lip (o), and immediately after that, the "bhujaṅga" (the letter ṅa).
At the end of *dhruva*, one should place the syllable mounted on *rakta* (the letter *r*), situated before the *pādita*;
at its head is the sixth, most excellent seed-syllable preceded by *ṛ*.
Furthermore, O Goddess Ambika,
one should write the fourth letter of the eleventh [varga], established in the color of tranquility (chānta), situated in the middle of the letter śu.
And before him is the deposition of the terrible form in the middle of the throat;
having extracted the syllable Jhaṇṭīśa, it is pierced by the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti).
Before that [first] seed-syllable is the letter beginning with 'na'; the second is established as the seed-syllable;
the third, the supreme seed-syllable, is preceded by 'ṛ' and joined with the lip [vowel].
One should place a serpent not joined with Ananta before him;
one should provide a seat beginning with Dhruva and draw "Me" in the center.
Having extracted the syllable *pra* with a fierce color (*pra*), it is joined with *ḷ* from the east;
the syllable situated in the middle of *śu* follows, together with the visarga at its end.
One should place Ghorā in front of him, established by the Hṛdinī;
having extracted Jñānaśakti, one places Ananta situated on the head.
Extracting the syllable beginning with *ṛ* (ṛkṣa) and so forth, join it with the *viśva* [syllable] and others;
likewise, take that which is situated at the end of the asterism (*bha*) within that very same *ṛṣimālā*.
Through union with the power of action, one should place the third, supreme seed-syllable—
the letter *visarga* in the color of semen (white)— before that.
The placement (*nyāsa*) associated with the terrifying color is in the center of the [letter] *bhu* (or *dara*);
*Mālinī* is situated on the left knee, arising from the powers of knowledge and action.
The first supreme seed-syllable is the fierce-colored one given at the head;
place the second, which belongs to the lower part, situated before it.
Having extracted the syllable of the Ṛṣi and others, adorned with the Viśva-syllable and so forth as its head,
one should place the beautiful syllable before it, which is the supreme abode of one's own Rudra.
Having taken the syllable produced from Umākānta, conjoined with Jhaṇṭīśena,
situated in the middle of the sword-crested [Sāsi], and originating from Bhairava and Śukra;
O Goddess, one should diligently perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon that which is joined with the end of the world, terrifying, and situated in front, located in the center of the navel.
Place that seed-syllable preceded by the five *praṇavas* before it; then place Ambikā, whose face is adorned with the letters of Mālinī, situated upon Mount Mandara.
Furthermore, O Goddess, one should extract Mahākāla alone;
before that is the white seed-syllable, where Bhairava is located at the end of the syllable Bhr̥gu.
One should write the fifth great seed-syllable conjoined with the Visarga;
having placed Vamanī in front, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon the secret parts.
Having extracted the power of action (kriyā-śakti), adorned with the Bindu at its head,
and [joined] Mālinī and the left foot situated at the beginning— O fair-faced one!
Halfway in front of him is the section beginning with Dhruva;
that which begins with 'Ya' is located in the Rudramālā, while the subtle one resides in the head.
Taking the supreme *snāyu* located in the middle of the left [channel],
O Goddess, one should draw that which is situated in the middle of the semen along with its emission.
Having placed Pāvanī in front, the placement on the anus (gudanyāsa) is proclaimed;
this very placement of the adamantine body (vajradeha) is indeed supremely difficult to attain.
"The Nyāsa residing in whose body is unassailable by gods or Daityas"—
thus, in the Pārameśvara-mata, is the twenty-eighth chapter, concerning the extraction of the three Vidyās and the Aghoryāṣṭaka.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
I shall now explain, in due order, the supreme deposition of the twelve [syllables].
Neither untimely death nor obstacles shall arise for him.
Freed from all diseases, he shall become equal to Rudra;
by means of the yoga beginning with the five *praṇavas*, one should extract the white-colored [syllable].
Place the seed-syllable of Bhṛgubhairava and Ambikā beneath it;
one should diligently extract these twelve locations.
It should be diligently differentiated according to the division of the twelve vowels:
the first [consonant] joined with the first [vowel], and the second with the second.
One should join the third with the third, the fourth with the fourth,
the fifth with the fifth, and apply the sixth to the sixth.
In the seventh [house], place the seventh; in the eighth, conjoin the eighth. And further, O Goddess, in the ninth [house], place the ninth before it.
In the tenth [chapter], perform the tenth [syllable] together with Rudra, and in the eleventh;
then again in the twelfth, O Goddess, perform it accompanied by the Visarga.
These twelve possess great power and are all joined with the *bindu*;
and Ambikā, the Great Goddess, is differentiated by these vowels.
The first utterance begins with the *praṇava* and is accompanied by the letter *sa*; it is called *siddhi*. The second is named *ṛddhi*.
The third is named Dyuti, the fourth is named Lakṣmī,
the fifth is Dīptimālī, and the sixth is proclaimed as Śivā.
Sumukhī is the seventh goddess, and Mālinī shall be the eighth;
Nandā is declared to be the ninth, and Hayavegā follows immediately after her.
In Rudra there is Mahāmukhī, and in Viśva there is Śāyī before her;
this is conjoined with two seed-syllables and preceded by the five *praṇavas*.

However, for each [mantra], one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) which grants the accomplishment of all goals: [one should place it] on the feet, knees, thighs, secret parts, navel, heart, throat, mouth, nostrils, ears, mantra, and head.
This is the twelve-limbed *nyāsa*; now hear the six-limbed [version].
Having extracted the Bhṛgubhairava mantra joined with five praṇavas,
[one should take] the first letter of Mālinī, where Vajriṇī is situated.
One should place the seed-syllable *tri* at the heart, mounted upon a horse of equal color, with one foot placed before Raktabhairava who stands upon its head.
The utterance of "namas" is established in the center of his heart;
O Goddess, it is on the peak of Kailāsa where Śrīkaṇṭha resides.
One should know the first syllable to be Mahākāla; before that is the second, most excellent syllable, mounted upon the fragment of the vowel Ṛ.
Having taken that which is situated in the middle of the *nāga*, mounted upon oneself,
and preceded by *ṛ*, the third supreme seed-syllable is placed upon the head.
O Goddess, one should draw the supreme trident of Mālinī situated in the midst of the twice-born (the letters),
joined with Sadyojāta, and likewise the fourth [letter].
O Goddess, one should draw the fifth [mandala], Viśvamālā, which is brought forth by yoga, located at the hips;
one should draw it in front of that [previous mandala] situated in the center of the world on Mount Mandara.
Having taken the letter situated below [the vowel], together with the *āṣāḍhī* of Bhairava,
and having placed it upon the head ending in *mandara*, this is the seventh, most excellent seed-syllable.
One should draw the eighth [deity], adorned with the color of Kailāsa, mounted upon Khaṇḍapāvaka, and surrounded by a garland of planets in their respective seasonal positions.
Having taken that which is situated in the midst of the waters, within the abode of the planets among the Rudras—
[the deity] Āṣāḍhī, mounted upon Bhairava, adorned with the colors of liberation.
One should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the head, joined with the word "svāhā" at the end;
likewise, the letters of the Mālinī [mantra] are for the throat (or mouth), while the sinews are the abode of Bhairava.
O Goddess, they say the first is the seed-syllable, adorned with the head [the letter *m*] and so forth;
the second is the consort of Rudra (*rudrāṇī*), situated between *kā*, *ū*, *ṛ*, and *dī*.
Furthermore, at the very beginning of this [mantra], one should extract the burning letter joined with the preceding vowel,
situated at the foot of Mālinī.
The Mālinī [mantra] is at the head, and the syllable of absolute liberation (kaivalya) adorned with the phonemes.
O Goddess, one should cause [the image] to be placed before him, situated upon the peak of Kailāsa,
having the color of a ram, and accompanied by Ananta.
Having extracted the seventh and placed the eighth in the position of Kānta, it is joined with Sūkṣmabhairava; now hear the ninth from me.
On Mount Mandara, situated in the midst of the elements, on its back is the supreme abode of Rudra;
conjoined with the end of Rudra is the ninth, most excellent seed-syllable.
One should know that the letter situated between *du* (and *dha*) is the supreme abode of Rudra, the Fish (*mīna*), which is the tenth; and that which ends with *vauṣaṭ* is the *śikhā*.
One should depict Mālinī with a complexion like that of the elements (bhūta), established in the color of the elements;
she should be shown holding the previously established color and engaged in recitation.
The third [seat] is Śūladaṇḍāsana, where Bhujaṅga is situated; it is pierced by the end of Mandara and belongs to Umākānta.
Its subtle essence is given as *śire* (or *śive*), which is established as absolute liberation (*kaivalya*).
Having extracted the fourth, most excellent letter from *pṛṣṭha* (or *pūṣṇi*) and *bhairava*, [one obtains it].
They know the fifth [letter] to be Jayantī mounted upon the letter Ra;
before that is the letter with the color of a fish (I), conjoined with Ananta.
One should first (seventh) draw the color of the Bhujangabhairava;
his ornament should be placed upon the head on Gandhamādana.
Then, O Goddess, Vāgīśa shall be the eighth and stand alone;
place the son of Bhṛgu (Ka) mounted upon the letter of the throat (Ū) of Mālinī.
Above the garland of syllables, the letter *ta* and so forth are established;
that too should be joined with a *bindu*, and its corresponding letter should be placed in front of it.
He too should make a red seat, established with the seed-syllable of Rudra;
one should know that to be the armor-mantra alone, established with the syllable *huṃ* at its end.
One should know that the first is the syllable situated in the midst of the elements, located at the mouth (or throat) of Mālinī; immediately after that is Saṃvartaka.
At the end of the *dhruva*, having grasped it below, it is situated in the middle of the six arms;
it is joined with the upward-pointing *uru* by the Lord and with the *krūra*.
And it is adorned, O lady of excellent hips; this is the third, most excellent seed-syllable, situated above the letter of the color of Śambhava.
Taking its beginning, the wise one should place it at the end of the *dhruva* while seated;
the fourth, most excellent seed-syllable is given for the head, extending to the end of the world.
Not joined with the visarga, white in color, it stands before that;
and the first letter [ca] is situated at the front of Kailāsa, standing upon its peak.
One should make the flesh, beginning with Dhruva and established in its seat, Bhairava;
one should know that the seventh is Mantu and the eighth is Lohita.
On the full moon day of Āṣāḍha, he was undoubtedly mounted by one with the appearance of Rudra;
holding nine locks of hair and a face, he stood in the midst of the dwelling.
One should know that alone as the ninth; there is no doubt in this.
Having extracted Krodhabhairava, perform the *nāgavyāsana*.
The subtle Rudra, the tenth supreme seed-syllable, is placed on the head;
through the union with the five praṇavas, "vaṣaṭ" is the supreme [syllable] for the eyes.
Make the letter *ja* its head, with that seed-syllable situated therein;
place the seat of the flesh of the fourth [vowel] in the eleventh position.
One should know that the first syllable is the Viśvamālā and others, inseparable, fierce, and situated at the head; Pāvanī stands before it.
Furthermore, O Goddess,
the fourth syllable is white in color, adorned with the letter *kṣe* at its end, situated upon the peak of Kailāsa, and most excellent.
The fifth seed-syllable is said to be the color arising from Meṣarudra, adorned with a head reaching to the end of the world; immediately after that is Āṣāḍhī.
Furthermore, O Goddess, one should draw the *saṃvaka* as the seventh;
then, starting from the eleventh, one should place Āṣāḍhī seated upon her throne in front.
At the end of *mandara*, O Goddess, is the eighth, supreme seed-syllable, undivided;
this is the supreme weapon-mantra (*astra*) for the six limbs, ending with *phaṭ*.
This body, composed of six sheaths, arises from Śiva and Śakti;
there is no doubt that for you, the impurity pertaining to seven lifetimes is destroyed.
I shall further explain how the placement of the knots (granthi-nyāsa) should be performed;
I shall tell you those which are the primordial seed-syllables (bīja) of all beings.
The letters beginning with 'a' and ending with the visarga, which arise from the Mātṛkā—
always perform the placement (nyāsa) of the knots, one by one, starting from the first among them.
O fair-faced one, first, that which is joined with the letter *ā* is on the fingers;
secondly, joined with the letter *sam*, it is the *kālagranthi*.

The placement (nyāsa) below the big toe and the ankle should be performed, which is most difficult to attain; it is declared that the "knot of the eldest" (jyeṣṭhagranthi) is joined with the third [finger] and so forth.
O lady of excellent complexion, the placement (nyāsa) should be performed situated in the middle of the two shanks;
the Raudri-knot is to be placed at the knee with the fourth [syllable] as the first.
Vāmadeva is proclaimed as being joined with the fifth [vowel];
having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) with effort, O Goddess, one should stand firmly with both feet with diligence.

O Goddess, one should place the sixth [syllable] located in the middle of the anus, which is the first utterance of the world, as the Brahma-knot; furthermore, O Goddess, one should deposit those [syllables] in the stations of Brahmā.
But with the seventh preceding vowel, O lady of excellent complexion,
the eighth is declared to be the "knot of desire" (kāmagranthi) in the middle of the secret place.
Perform the initial utterance with the eighth seed-syllable;
then, by means of the ninth seed-syllable, one should place the lunar knot (somagranthi).
The region situated below the navel is completely filled like the moon;
O Goddess, one should then place the solar knot (sūryagranthi) in the center of the navel.
O woman of excellent complexion, one should perform [the rite] with the tenth preceding [syllable];
the eleventh seed-syllable stands in the middle of the womb.
O Goddess of the Suras, one should diligently perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon the vital knot in the heart,
which is endowed with twelve [syllables] and contains the knot of the life-force (jīvagranthi).
One should know the Viṣṇu-knot as the thirteenth at the location of the throat;
one should diligently perform the placement (nyāsa) of the Rudra-knot as the fourteenth.
Established in the middle of the palate by means of the fourteenth seed-syllable, one performs the placement of the knot of Īśa; the seed-syllable is then formed by the fifteenth.
One should know that it resides in the forehead; above that is the sixteenth digit (kalā) of the god Sadāśiva, established as the form of the knot.
The placement of the knots (granthinyāsa) is proclaimed by means of the division of the sixteen digits;
furthermore, there is the supreme placement of Ambikā consisting of twelve [syllables].
I shall now fully explain that supreme means for achieving great siddhi,
having extracted Śukrabhairava, who is seated upon the staff of the trident.
Above that is the goddess Ambikā; this great seed-syllable of Kuṭa should be extracted with effort for the twelve locations.
It should be diligently differentiated by means of the twelve vowel distinctions;
indeed, each single vowel, beginning with *a* and ending with the *visarga*, [should be applied].
In the first [case], it is proclaimed as the "Name of Accomplishment" (Siddhināmā) through the application of seed-syllables;
one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) on the feet, which bestows all accomplishments.

By means of the second seed-syllable, one becomes the very powerful [deity] named Ṛddhi; one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) here, and there is no doubt that success will be attained. (For the sake of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*), the placement on the knees should be performed; of this there is no doubt.)
O Goddess of the gods, having performed the placement [of mantras] upon the middle of the thighs with the eastern wheel using the seed-syllable *rā*,
I shall now describe the supreme *aghornī* placement, which effects the attraction of all things.
The fourth [center] is situated in the middle of the anus, where Lakṣmī resides;
one should diligently perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) as the means for propitiating Mahālakṣmī.
The placement at the navel is established by the fifth seed-syllable;
she is the goddess named Dīpti, the bestower of the lamp of knowledge.
O Goddess, situated in the center of the heart, she abides beginning with the sixth seed-syllable;
she is named Māyā, supreme and subtle, the awakener of all illusion.
Relying upon the seventh seed-syllable, situated in the middle of the throat of Śivā,
that [syllable] which brings peace to Śivā is to be installed there, O Goddess, according to the rule.
The goddess named Sumukhī is established in the eighth seed-syllable;
this placement performed in the center of the mouth is supreme for achieving perfection in speech.
By means of the ninth seed-syllable, which is the primordial self,
one performs the supreme placement (nyāsa) of the nose, entering the city [of the body].
From the two eyes, the auspicious goddess Nandinī, who brings joy to all, was manifested;
by the tenth [digit], Pūrvā, she was established as Dūradarśanī.
The one with golden hair and great strength, Durāśravaṇā, when placed by means of the eleventh seed-syllable in the middle of the ears, performs [her function].
Situated on the crown of the head in the twelfth [center], she who possesses great hair is firmly established;
she bestows dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation, and grants the accomplishment of all goals through the ritual placement (nyāsa).
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, concerning the twelve-limbed and six-limbed ritual placement of Ambikā, according to the Pārameśvara doctrine.
The illustrious Bhairava said: Furthermore, I shall proclaim another supreme placement (nyāsa) extracted from that [tantra],
by the mere performance of which all accomplishments (siddhi) arise.
Śrīkaṇṭha, the goddess Nādinī, and the third seed-syllable, Parā; Ananta, the goddess Grasanī, and the third seed-syllable, born from Parā.
Sūkṣmarudra and Nivṛtti, as well as Vidyā, are situated at the end of the seed-syllables;
for Pratiṣṭhā, there are Trimūrti and the others, with the supreme seed-syllable at the end.
For the Vidyā of Amarīśā and the others, [the mantra consists of] the third [letter], the fifth of the subsequent group,
Arghīśa, Śānti situated before [it], and the third Māyā-bīja.
One should write Bhārabhūti and Cāmuṇḍā as the seventh of the others;
having placed Atithi in the east, Priyadarśanī is situated in the middle.
At its end, one should extract the eighth seed-syllable, which is red;
then, O Goddess, Nārāyaṇī is established as Sthāṇvīśa at the beginning.
At its end, they say there is the syllable "rakta" (red), which is the supreme among the supreme;
it is the deluding seed-syllable of Hari, the letter "ma," standing at the forefront.
The syllable originating from Jhaṇṭīrudra is situated in the middle for the sake of Prajñā;
at its end, one should extract the eighth seed-syllable, which is red, and the seed-syllable of Rudra belonging to the Supreme should be declared.
One should know that previously there was the secret power (guhyaśakti) before that; the wise man should write the supreme seed-syllable (parābīja) and the twelfth [syllable] without any doubt.
Furthermore, O Goddess, Sadyojāta is situated in the center of Vajriṇī;
and again, O Goddess, the third is the seed-syllable of Parā, the thirteenth.
The Lord of Grace is in the east, and Kālī is situated in the middle;
at its end is the supreme seed-syllable, the fourteenth seed-syllable which should be bestowed.
Furthermore, O Goddess, Kapālī, who is of a cruel appearance, is situated in the middle;
one should then cause him to receive that fifteenth seed-syllable of Parā.
One should place Śivā in the center and Mahāsena at the beginning;
the sixteenth supreme seed-syllable is situated after the third.
Having first extracted Krodha, and immediately after that Ghorā,
O Goddess, one should then place the seventeenth seed-syllable, Parā, in front of it.
First is Pracaṇḍabhairava; [the goddess] is situated in the middle of the two excellent [syllables].
Then follows the third of the eighteen, which is the arising of the supreme seed-syllable (parābīja).
They know Pracaṇḍabhairava to be in the east and Sarasvatī in the center;
at the end of that, O Goddess, one should again extract Parājaya.
Having first written the syllable Śiva, one should place the syllable Vāgeśvarī in the middle;
then, one should cause the third, the supreme seed-syllable (Parā-bīja), to be placed before it.
One should place Mahārudra with one foot in the center, while Śikhivāhinī is at its end;
and at the very end of that, the twenty-first [syllable] Parā should be assigned.
One should diligently perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of Kūrmabhairava situated in the east, Bhīmā stationed in the center, and the third, which is the supreme seed-syllable (parābīja).
O Goddess, one should again place the first [syllable] of Vāyuvega as the single hand (or eye);
and the third, the supreme seed-syllable, should certainly be assigned.
The name and the supreme seed-syllable situated in the center of the wheel,
joined with the four-faced one (the letter *Ha*) and placed at the beginning— this is the most excellent ritual placement (*nyāsa*).
One should cause the goddess named Vināyakī to be placed in front of Bhairava, who is established as the primordial one, born from the left shoulder.
Furthermore, fashion the third [syllable] as the seed-syllable of Parā;
it should be preceded by Sarvabhairava and situated in the middle of Pūrṇimā.
The third [deity] situated in front is born from supreme knowledge (*parāvidyā*).
One should place Someśvara in the east; they know Jhaṃkāriṇī to be in the center.
The third seed-syllable should be given, extracted from the supreme vidyā;
O Goddess, Lāṅgalīśa is again established in the east by means of the Kurdanī.
One should write the third seed-syllable of Parā at its end;
preceded by Dārubhairava, it is situated in the middle of Dīpinī.
One should diligently extract the seed-syllable of the adversary from its front;
[one should place] the Lord Ardhānārīśvara and Jayantī situated in the east.
One should draw the third letter, which arises from the seed of supreme knowledge (parāvidyā).
Having extracted the initial seed-syllable, one should [draw] Bhairava, the beloved of Umā.
Kapālī is in the Middle Country; the third is Parodbhava;
and Āṣāḍhībhairava is situated in the center of Pavanī in the east.
The third seed-syllable of Parā should be extracted with great care;
Ambikā is she who was previously established as Diṇḍibhairava.
At the end of Ambikā, one should extract the third [vowel] and the seed-syllable of Parā;
[the letters] Dhātrīśa, Bhairava, and Pūrva, and Mahāsena (and Icchāśakti) situated in the middle.
O lady of excellent complexion, one should draw the seed-syllable of Parā as the third;
Mīnarudra is in the east, while Sarmmarudra is of great power.
The third [syllable] is to be extracted, as is the great seed-syllable of the Supreme;
it is situated before Meṣabhairava and resides in the middle of Chāgalī.
And the third seed-syllable of Parā should be placed before that;
O Goddess, the red Bhairavī is situated to the east of the Puta.
The seed-syllable before [it] is the third, arising from the Supreme Goddess (Parādevī);
Śikhivāhinī and Mahārudra, along with Āṣāḍhī, are situated in the center.
At its end, the supreme seed has arisen and remains, which is difficult to obtain;
furthermore, O Goddess, they know the "goat's testicle" (chagalaṇḍa) to be at its end, hanging down.
One should recognize the third [syllable] as *parāvara*; of this there is no doubt.
Having offered oblation to Bhairava, who is twice-egg-shaped (*dviraṇḍa*), she becomes the Withdrawer (*saṃhāriṇī*) in the center.
The third seed-syllable of Parā should be extracted with effort;
Rudra is in the east, and Mahākāla and Mahākālī are situated in the center.
At the end of that, the seed-syllable of Parā must certainly be extracted;
Vāgīśa-Bhairava is at the beginning, and Kusumāyudha is situated at the end.
The seed-syllable of the Supreme should be extracted with effort at the end;
Bhujaṅgabhairava is first, while the Goddess is situated in the middle.
The third, the seed-syllable of Parā, should be extracted with effort.
They say Vināyakī is in the east, while Tārā is situated in the center.
Place the third seed-syllable of Parā at its end;
O Goddess, Khaḍgīśa Bhairava and Jñānaśakti are situated in the east.
Having extracted the third [vowel] and the seed-syllable of the Supreme,
and having extracted the *saṃvartaka* [fire], the power of action (*kriyāśakti*) resides in the center.
One should cause the third [syllable] of *parā* to be placed at the end of that;
the *gāyatrī* is situated in the middle, preceded by *Śvetabhairava*.
But for another, let him diligently perform the third [rite] at its conclusion;
Sāvitrī is in the middle region, while Bhṛgu is situated in the east.
One should draw the third [syllable] of the other, and at its end, one should write Lakulīśabhairava; the first [syllable] is Dahanī, situated in the middle.
It should be extracted with effort, and at its end is Parā;
Saṃvartaka Mahārudra is situated in the eastern part.

In the center is the goddess Phetkāriṇī; the third [mantra] ending with the three vidyās, the goddess’s sacrificial thread (yajñopavīta), and the ritual placement (nyāsa) which bestows perfection upon all limbs.
O lady of excellent complexion, one should perform the pacification of all obstacles.
O Rudra, those letters beginning with 'a' and ending with 'kṣa' are born from you.
O Goddess, each one of its preceding utterances is established;
make Mālinī situated in the middle, beginning with the letter *na* and ending with the letter *pha*.
The supreme, the inferior, and likewise the intermediate;
within these three branches of knowledge are the fifty seed-syllables.
One should perform the deposition (nyāsa) of each individual letter of the alphabet arising from the Mālinī, positioned before oneself,
having formed the mass of sounds (śabdarāśi) and joined it with the Bhairavas of the letters.
Furthermore, the goddess Mālinī was deposited together with the Yoginī;
likewise, the goddess Parā, Aparā, and Parāparā were deposited.
O Goddess, whatever placement (*nyāsa*) was previously performed regarding all other mantras,
all of that becomes fruitless without the seizing (*grahaṇa*).
The sacrificial thread, placed upon the goddess according to the rules of ritual, becomes endowed with seed-syllables;
and whatever was performed previously in the former month, all that likewise becomes possessed of seed-syllables.
Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, concerning the extraction of that [mantra], according to the Pārameśvara-mata.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully declare twelve verses,
by the mere knowledge of which one is liberated from all sins.
O Goddess, in the temple of Arghīśa, [the Linga] is established with the lower syllable;
one should cause the *pūrveṇiṣa* to be placed upon its head.
The goddess Kusumāyudhā should cause his color to be placed above;
one should know this to be the primordial seed-syllable (ādibīja) situated upon the serpent—of this there is no doubt.

In the eleventh Ṛṣisthāna, Mālinī is located at the throat; she should be extracted with effort from both locations above that. In the location immediately preceding that, [one should extract] Tadagra.
Furthermore, that seed-syllable should then be placed in front, seated upon the seat of fire;
