beneath it, one should provide the letter *śa*, conjoined with the half-moon (*ardhacandra*).
One should cause the semen born from Mālinī to be placed upon his head;
in the temple of Bhūtamālā, the letter situated in the east [is to be applied].
The letter *ri* (and the nine others) mounted upon [the vowels], with the letter *ṛ* situated at the head,
and adorned by the distinctions of the letters beginning with *la*, shall be the fifth.
Having extracted the syllable *huṃ* along with the end of the world,
it is named Rudrasaṃvartaka and is situated at the end of the seed-syllable of all beings.
This six-syllabled vidyā is the primordial element in the Kula-āgama;
herein, in its midst, twelve verses have arisen.
Listen to how it occurs through the distinction of fifty letters:
the seed-syllable of the second Vidyā is established in each preceding position.
And at its end, O Goddess, you should likewise arrange that same color;
and one should have these golden [elements] fashioned in the positions of the yugas.
One should cause the syllables arising from the Mātṛkā to be given in each of the solitary places;
likewise, the second and the third, as well as whatever seed-syllables of the Vidyās there may be.
Each successive letter of the alphabet must be performed one by one;
beginning with the letter *a* and ending with *sa*, this purifying process leads to the attainment of fullness.
Thus indeed these twelve verses were previously spoken by the Lord;
whoever recites them, or to whose ear they are imparted, those ears become instructors.
For these are indeed secret and most secret; one should write them down using a book.
This six-syllable vidyā must not be given to just anyone.
It must be given even to one who is uninitiated or a reviler of the Kula path;
however, if it is given through negligence, the loss of spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*) occurs.
One should diligently perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of Mekhalā and Kubjikā;
for [otherwise] there are spirits, ghosts, and piśācas, as well as fearsome, wicked fanged ones (or bandits).
Among them are the messengers Yama-citra and Vicitra, who possess great strength;
they [deal] with one devoid of life-force and with one who is pure despite his sin.
O lady of excellent hips, he is unable even to look upon his own face;
having conquered the messengers of Yama, he goes to the world of Rudra.
Now I shall further explain another [method]: there are twelve [centers] in the body;
one should pierce them from below and above using the steps and the root-instruments.
One should cause the throbbing channel, which has the form of the flame of a lamp’s wick, to enter;
having reached the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), it reaches Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Śiva.
Consciousness is immortal and divine, bestowing the fruits of the fourfold aims of life;
it resides in the upper nasal cavity, extending as far as the abode of the expanse of space.
The supreme power (Paramāśakti) stands above, raining down the supreme nectar;
she is as lovely as a digit of the moon’s orb and possesses the luster of purified gold.
One should meditate upon the Self, dissolved from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head;
with the gaze fixed on the tip of the nose, one should savor the supreme nectar of reality.
O Goddess, having drawn back the lips into the shape of a crow's beak in a wondrous manner, the Self becomes the equal flavor, the supreme nectar in the primordial place.
This samādhi bestows purity upon the body;
having sprinkled nectar upon every limb, it establishes the physical form of the body therein.
Then, O Dear One, having daily deposited that state of phonemes and words— both external and internal—
upon the two equal planes of dharma and adharma.
One should apply within one's own body the yoga that destroys death—
the supreme reality ending in the Nāda, from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head.
He who perceives the oneness equal to the sun and the moon is liberated;
he may rise up and fall down again, yet he shall eventually ascend to the state of Rudreśvara.
The knower of the instruction on *nāda* attains the eternal state;
through the agitation of the two organs, [the breaths] reside between the moon and the sun.
When the bindu has emerged, it has then attained that state of excellence;
the supreme bindu has emerged as a constant flow like the sun.
And those who drink [this] become liberated; they go to the supreme goal.
O Goddess, these twelve verses were previously heard by me.
O Goddess, these were spoken by me and have emerged from my own self.
Ten verses have been cited in connection with the *Pañcaratna*.
"The two [states] in the state of non-referentiality (nirālamba-pada) thus make twelve that have been proclaimed.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"Now I shall further proclaim those which are the five jewels."
O Sovereign of the Gods, this ritual placement (nyāsa) has been performed for the sake of purifying the five locations.
Then, having taken that which is situated in the middle among the planets in the abode of the elements,
the *śikhā* is established in the middle of the eleventh and the fourth.
And having extracted the second [letter],
one should place the letter arising from Mahākāla, which stands at the tip of that *pavanī*, before him.
The letter at the head of Mālinī is the fifth; of this there is no doubt.
Adorn these five letters with Lokādi.
"Having observed that which is situated in the middle of the world, one should apply it below;
they are mounted by Arghīśa and adorned by Lokānta.
The syllable situated between the eyebrows belongs to Pinākin and Bhairava."
All those mounted there are seated upon the throne of Arghīśa.
One should place these five jewels in five locations:
first, the moon mandala is situated at the center of the head.
A great lotus with sixteen petals, hanging with its face turned downwards, shining like jasmine or the moon; in its center is the pericarp.
Therein, the syllable situated in the center is the first and supreme jewel;
it consists of the sixteen digits (kalās), beginning with the letter 'A' and ending with the visarga.
The wise practitioner should visualize [the deity] raining down white-colored nectar from the rays of the full moon, which are established at the tips of the petals.
Then, one should contemplate oneself situated in the center of that lotus,
merged like a lamp through the first application of the jewel.
By this yoga of practice, after six months, gray hair is destroyed;
after one year, divine splendor and a great body are produced.
O Goddess, in sixteen years there is no doubt that one attains the state of moving through the sky;
I shall now describe those who have attained perfection through the yoga of the first sequence.
O fair-faced one, sixty-four crores of Siddhas together with Yoginīs, remaining in the sky, exercise their authority.
The second [lotus] is situated in the center of the heart; it has eight petals and is very beautiful (and possesses a pericarp).
It has the luster of white and yellow colors, and the pericarp is situated in the middle.
Therein, one should meditate upon the second supreme jewel situated in the center:
sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as the fifth.
O lady of excellent complexion, with effort place the mind, the intellect, and the ego— one by one— upon the petals, and place the Self in the center.
O Goddess of gods, those qualities which arise in a single year are the knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the vision of what is distant.
By practicing through this sequential yoga, O Goddess, there is no doubt;
within twelve years, one attains perfection—of this there is no doubt.
In former times, fifty crores of yoginīs, together with the siddhas, were granted authority by me; now established in heaven, they sport there.
Furthermore, the wheel located at the navel, resting upon a lotus with six petals, is entirely composed of red and white; in its center is a third jewel.

O Goddess, one should contemplate that [object] until one has attained absorption in it;

One speaks all the scriptures, even those not seen or heard before, and enters the bodies of others; of this there is no doubt.
The Siddhakhecarī has been described as being twenty-seven years old;

O Varārohā, in the netherworld (pātāla) below this [earth], there are those who hold authority;

In its center is a triangle, resembling the red glow of vermilion; it is situated in the womb (yoni), supremely divine, and from it the entire world of moving and non-moving beings was born.
One should meditate upon that fourth, supreme jewel situated in its center—
divine, producing great radiance, and illuminating all things moving and stationary.
Dissolve the self into that very place in its subtle form;

Shaking, trembling, horripilation, bliss, and even dizziness; divine speech, arrival of sleep, and the movement of the vital breaths—these are established [as signs].
Through the yoga of constant practice, mastery over speech arises,

Within twelve years, however, the visible becomes invisible;

Through this yoga of practice, I shall tell you of the accomplishment attained together with the Yoginīs of eighteen crores of Siddhas.

O beloved, there is a three-petaled lotus, variegated in form and white and red in color; in its center, O dear one, [the seed-syllable] has arisen, resembling a bamboo sprout.

In this wheel, however, are those who have attained accomplishment, possessing the great power of eighty million; they are the lords of the world of the *nāgas*, together with thousands of accomplished *yoginīs*.

The Goddess said: "O Lord, I have heard the remainder of the *nyāsa*, which is most difficult to obtain.

To one who is of noble birth and endowed with courage,

The supreme heart of Kālikā consists of the syllable *bhū* (bh), followed by *ā*, then *ma*, *nda*, *ra*, *si*, *va*, *da*, *ya*, *vā*, *ja*, *va*, *ra*, and *pa*; it is conjoined with a *bindu* at its head. This is the supreme [mantra].
Having extracted the seed-syllable beginning with 'ha', one should place the letter 'ī' in the middle of its tip.

The three seed-syllables are said to be presided over by the fierce head;
furthermore, O Goddess, in front of that is the syllable of wrath, which is red in color.
The nineteenth seed-syllable is combined with the stable middle [vowel];
then, having extracted Krodha again, Kha is situated above and below.
The letter situated in the middle of *kīra*, with *Umākānta* (Ha) placed upon its head,
joined with *Jhaṃṭīśa* (Ra), and preceded by the letter of *Vajriṇī* (Va).
The seed-syllable consisting of twenty-seven [phonemes] should have its head severed by Viśva and the others;

Taking the nineteenth [letter],

Having extracted [the mantra] from the midst of the *veśa*, it is established upon the seat of Bāli;

The twentieth seed-syllable, increased by two, is situated within the living being;

Seated in the serpent-posture (bhujaṅgāsana), with the seed-syllable of Vajriṇī before him,
joined with the letter preceding *ḷ*, this is the excellent thirty-sixth seed-syllable.
And at the beginning, the Praṇava should be placed in reverse order as previously indicated;
this is the Goddess Mahākālī, possessing the brilliance of the fire that consumes time.
Endowed with qualities such as omniscience and bestowing the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation,
this Goddess of the Gods of gods must not be given to one who does not possess the body of Bhairavī.
Formerly, by me as Gopīna, [this was proclaimed] among Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Īśvara, and the others,
and among the gods, dānavas, siddhas, yakṣas, and gandharvas.
Hidden among the Nāgas and the wives of the Nāgas, this goddess is difficult to find on earth;
he who bestows her upon his guru gains [merit] throughout the three worlds.
Nothing is to be withheld from him, including his own self, wife, and so forth;
O Goddess, I have now revealed to you even that which is secret among secrets.
O Goddess, O beloved, this must be kept secret by you in every way and at all times;
having first uttered the Praṇavas and then the Kūṭa... [and so forth].
Having extracted the first letter *u* and placed it at the end of *ga*,
one places the seed-syllable of Rakta below it, and Pūtanā is situated beneath that.
One should place the liquor of the seed-syllable of Krodha in the middle of that flame;
below that, in the middle of the *chaṅga* vessel, situated upon the seat ending with the *dhruva*.
Below that is Raktabīja, and Pūtanā stands holding him;
his name is joined with the letter 'a' at its end and marked by the digit of the nasal bindu.
O Goddess, this Kūṭarāja, which destroys gods and dānavas,
the secret heart of the Śākinīs, has been declared by me to you out of devotion.
For one who has performed recitation, fire-offerings, and meditation for a number of one million six hundred thousand times,
restraint proceeds by his mere will.
Having taken Meṣarudra and Mahākāla before him,
one should join the second king of seed-syllables with Sadyojāta.
Having taken Dviraṇḍabhairava and Pracaṇḍa before him,
[one should place] Vajriṇī in the seed-mantra (bījamantra), and Āṣāḍhī immediately after that.
The head of Viśvādin (Vi) is split; the king of seeds (Sa) is endowed with Rasa (E). Having extracted the middle syllable (Ṛ), Kaṣānta (Ha) is situated before it.
And that which is situated on the seat of Someśvara is proclaimed as being equal in number to the Vasus;
thereafter, one should offer Kūrmarudra together with Ananta.
The letter *ṭha* at the end, pierced by the *nāda*, the *bindu*, and the *śiras*;
then, joined with the letter *ṛ* at its end, followed by *pinākī*.
Taking the seed-syllable of Rudra, which is joined with the Viśvādi [mantra] and is unvoiced (*asvara*),
one should grasp the Bhairava of the Serpents (*Bhujaṅgabhairava*) established upon the seat beginning with Dhruva.
Taking up Mīnarudra, adorned by Mandara,
and holding the trident-staff of Mālinī, he placed Mahākāla before him.
One should place the Ananta [mantra], conjoined with the Bindu, upon its head;
thereafter, one should place Bhṛṅgabhairava alone in front of it.
From that comes Dviraṇḍa Bhairava, and immediately after that, Saṃvarta;
preceded by the letter *i*, [one worships] Umākānta, the fierce one.
Taking Krodhabhairava, one should place "O" at its beginning;

Then, having extracted Lakulīśa, one should place Meṣarudra before him;
O fair lady, he should be divided into two parts, and Dahanī should be placed before him.
Furthermore, O Sovereign of the Gods, one should place Lakulīśa at the end in two ways;
having extracted [the syllable] and joined it with the letter 'A'.
His [form] is terrifying with serpents and adorned by Mandara;
then one should place Mīnarudra, and before him, Mahākāla. O Great Goddess, one should likewise make two forms: Lohita and Kūrma.
The seed-syllable *grasa* is twofold, joined with *huṃ phaṭ* at the end and *svāhā*;

Whether in a cremation ground, under a solitary tree, on a riverbank, or at a confluence of rivers,
he who stands firm in the vow of a hero should recite this vidyā one hundred thousand times.
The enemies such as fever and disease are utterly destroyed for him;
indeed, intense power over both restraint and favor arises.
O Goddess, what more need be said? The power of the Goddess is truly wondrous;
by the mere remembrance of her, there is the destruction of fevers, malevolent spirits, and other afflictions.
Furthermore, I shall describe another supreme means for bringing her into one's presence:
one should especially offer oblations of *mahāphalgu* soaked in clarified butter.
O Goddess, this [mantra] is declared to be threefold; one should extract Śivodūtī [from it].
It must not be given to just anyone who does not possess a portion of the heroic nature (vīrāṃśa).
Having extracted the Praṇava and so forth, [the syllable] Āṣāḍhī follows immediately thereafter.
Below that, the Goddess (Devī) should be placed, conjoined with Sadyojāta;
taking the seed-syllable of Pūtanā, it is adorned by that which resides on Mount Mandara.
One should draw this [diagram] with its infinite extent at the front and the center;
then, one should write the fifth supreme seed-syllable, which is conjoined with the letter *ṛ* at its head.
Then, having extracted Mahākāla, who is seated upon the seat of Soma,
his head is pierced by the syllable *ṛ*, with *ṛ* situated at the end.
Furthermore, O Bhadrā, Lakulīśa is situated in Vajriṇī and Īśvara;
[the syllable] consisting of the letter of Bhṛgu (B) joined with the Bindu (Ṃ), standing before Chagalaṇḍa (U).
Then, having extracted Someśvara and adorned it with Mandara,
Ananta should be placed at the end, marked by the Bindu and the digit of the moon.
Taking the seed-syllable of Fire (Ra), adorned by the letter Niṣadha (Sa) standing upon it,
one should place the end of Ṛ at the end, augmented by the digit of the moon and the bindu.
Having first drawn Dhruva and the others, one should draw Pinākin immediately after that.
Jhaṃṭīśa is placed at the head; the syllable Ṛ is situated before it and below it.
It is not different when located on Mandara, and in the mantra it is joined with Ananta.
Above Pūtanā is the great seed-syllable; then again, the Vajrayudhā mantra.
Below that is the beloved [syllable] taken from Kā, conjoined with Dhruva (Oṃ) and the others.
One should place the full moon (O) below the letter Ṭha, which bestows all accomplishments;
having extracted the center of the syllable Bha, it stands before Pūtanā.
Taking the bindu from the solar ray (ravi-rci), O God, one should place it beneath that; it is pierced by that which resides on Mandara and is situated at the end as Ananta.
And at the end, one should offer the five deities in reverse order.
This goddess is a great secret, renowned by the name Bhellakhī.
Through the application of the oil sacrifice for the sake of deluding all sentient beings, this is declared as a great secret; it should not be given to just anyone.
At the beginning, one should draw the Full Moon and the second [digit] (the New Moon); at their end, one should write the red seed-syllable of Wrath.
Having taken up the seed-syllable of Wrath, one should indeed be seated upon the Āṣāḍhī [seat].
The syllable of the Vedas was uttered by Jhaṃṭīśa with his heads shattered;
thereafter, he took up Mahākāla and struck Ambikā.
The seed-syllable of taste (ra) is proclaimed as being joined with the infinite (a).
Having extracted the serpent-seed (sa), the seed of wrath (kṣa) follows thereafter.
For one should take Āṣāḍhī, who is mounted upon her seat and distinguished by the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti),
and from there [take] Mahākāla, who is situated in the center.
Having taken [the seed-syllable] situated between *ṭha* and *dū*, which has ascended to the seat beginning with *dhruva*, is afflicted by *krūra* at the head,
and is joined with *jhaṃṭīśa*;
Having taken the syllable *bhṛgu* (ṃ), situated upon the seed-syllable seat of *vajra* (ha),
and having grasped the *vālīśa* seed-syllable (sa) located between *ra* and *la* in front;
The seed-syllable (bīja) is split at the head by the vowel *ṛ* and so forth, with the number of worlds [fifteen];
this great goddess-vidyā is celebrated as Netrapūtī.
O fair-faced one, by means of the yoga of the five *praṇavas* at the beginning and the end,
one should extract this vidyā, which accomplishes all desires and aims.
Now, therefore, I shall fully proclaim the Great Vidyā, O Great Goddess, known by the name Astradūtī, which accomplishes all rites.
Having grasped him situated in the midst of the *taṇu*, established upon the preeminent seat,
the goddess Ambikā stood before him, seated upon her own central throne.
In front of that, the seed-syllable of Wrath (KṢA) is situated upon the letter E;
having taken the seed-syllable of Vajrīṇī (HRĪM), O Dear One, it is placed in the middle of the syllable KĪ.
The fourth seed-syllable, which is unconfused and supreme, is located at the tip of the mandara;
having grasped it starting from the eleventh [position], it is adorned with the power of gnosis (jñāna-śakti).
Having grasped that which is situated in the center of the jar, established upon the seat beginning with Dhruva,
the seed-syllable of the Trailokyadaṃara, joined with Nāda, Bindu, and Kalā.
Furthermore, the first syllable of the *Ṛṣi* [meter] should be placed as the left foot of the *Mālinī*;
this should be made to fall after the seventh syllable.
One should take the two Mahākālas situated between the *īṣā* vowels and extract them;
then, having taken them from the middle of the *cāva* vowels, they were spoken by Bhujaṅga.
In the Sadyojāta [face], one should take that undivided seed-syllable known as Īśvara, which is situated between *pā* and *na*; and before it is the burner (*dahanī*).
The serpent, mounted upon Bhairava, is proclaimed to be of universal color;
having extracted the color of the sinews, it is endowed with Ananta.
Having taken that which is situated in the center of the atom (the *bindu*) and placed it upon the staff of the trident (*śūla*),
one should then extract the syllable *Tārā* and adorn it with the flower-weapon (*kusumāyudha*).
Again, having given the preceding syllable, twenty phonemes are prescribed;
taking that which is situated in the mind, it is established upon the seat ending with the *dhruva*.
Having taken the first, middle, and last [letters], with the letter *ra* placed upon the head,
one should extract the seed-syllable of the Wind, seated upon the throne of the serpent.
Having taken the letter *pa* situated between *pā* and *mo*, it is joined with *sa* from *sadyojāta*;
then, having taken the letter *kha* situated between *khī* and *nū*, it is endowed with *na* from *anaṃta*.
Having taken the seed-syllable of Fire (Ra), adorned with the letter situated on Mount Mandara (Ma),
one should then extract the seed-syllable of Wrath (Hūṃ), which is fashioned by the Cruel One (Kṛ).
One should grasp that which is situated in the middle of the *vevū*, adorned with the portion of the *ṛśa*;
thereafter, it is of the color of a ram and endowed with the fire of the color of wrath.
Having extracted the seed-syllable of Tārā and joined it with the nasal drop (bindu), one should place the letter *ca*.
Then, taking the first letter after *da*, which is situated above *ḷ*.
Then, having extracted the letter *tha* situated below it and joined it with *na*,
one should take the letter *gha* located between *tha* and *ha* and adorn it with the letter situated on *ma*.
The thirty-fifth seed-syllable is that Tārā together with the nasal drop (bindu);
having extracted the first of the eleven [vowels], it is then conjoined with the serpent (the letter *sa*).
When pierced in the head by a cruel [weapon], it is remembered as the thirty-eighth.
Having extracted the ninth [letter] from after Nāra (i.e., the letter *ū*), it is established upon the seat of the vowel *ī*;
then, having placed the middle of *ka* (the letter *ṣ*) from there, it is joined below with *adhaḥ*.
The thirty-eighth [syllable] is remembered as being pierced in the head by the cruel one;
having extracted the second *tārā* (OM), it is joined with the seat of the letter *ī*.
Then, O Dear One, having given the color of a ram, one should cause it to fall;
and before that, O Vajriṇī, there should be the seed-syllable of Bhṛṅgabhairava.
One should cause that [disc] to be made as stepped upon by the serpent Ananta, adorned with ornaments, and fallen before Śiva along with Mālinī.
One should place two *hara*-seeds and then write the syllables of Rudra;
having given the word *karāline*, one should then extract the three seeds.
Then there is the Heart of Cāmuṇḍā, followed by the King of Mudrās;
taking the feet of Kubjikā, it is always preceded by the secret [syllable].
Conjoined with *huṃ phaṭ* at the end and followed by *svāhā*, she is proclaimed as the Queen of Vidyās.
Whoever recites this vidyā and especially performs oblations with it—
O Goddess, one shall become a conqueror of the three worlds; this is the truth, there is no doubt.
First is the placement of the *praṇava*, and second is the nine-fold self.
The third [part] of Trikhaṇḍā is indeed the Samaya-ātman;
the fourth is the Śabdarāśi; and the sixth is remembered as Mālinī.
The seventh is indeed the Threefold Knowledge (Trividyā), the eighth is the Aghoryāṣṭaka;
the ninth is the Twelve Limbs (Dvādaśāṅga), while the tenth is known as the Six Limbs (Ṣaḍaṅga).
The eleventh [type of] nyāsa is known as that which is joined with sixteen knots;
the twelfth is to be understood as the twelfth, and the thirteenth belongs to the graha.
The placement known as "the worlds" (bhuvana) is proclaimed in twelve verses;
the placement of the five jewels (ratnapañcaka) is recorded in fifteen [verses].
The six messengers are to be known as the sixteenth; this is remembered as the sixfold deposition (ṣoḍhā-nyāsa).
He who, firm in his vows and with a purified body, performs this deposition at the three junctions of the day, [attains success].
"By the falling of his glance, even mountains are shattered.
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, titled "The Extraction of the Five Jewels of Twelve Verses," according to the Pārameśvara-mata.
The Goddess said:
I have heard those twelve verses, both external and internal,
as well as the stainless instruction on the five jewels from him.
Now I wish to hear the worship of the Krama,
by the mere knowledge of which the accomplishment of the Command proceeds.
How can that power, which is supreme, subtle, and established as the Mother of the World,
be one measure, two measures, or three measures?
The supreme, subtle half-mora, established within the half of which letter does it reside?
O Lord, how is it that she is established in the form of a vulva (bhaga) and as a half-liṅga?
Churned by Bhairava through the differentiation of the state of Nirvāṇa,
the Great Goddess known as the syllable *Ku* is established there in the center.
Arising from the power of Rudra in the form of Ājñāsana,
how is the sixfold [system] perfected, and how are the four seats (pīṭhas) established?
O Lord, how do the goddesses of the seats (pīṭhas) abide together with the Siddhis?
In what place did they originate, and what is called the Brahma-knot?
O Lord, what is the nature of the *sakala* (with parts), and how does the *niṣkala* (without parts) come to be?
What is described as the different types of liberation that is devoid of existence and non-existence?
Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as the fifth— these elements,
together with the mind situated within the mass of the six chakras, are firmly established.
One knows the specific quality of each of the sense organs in their respective locations;
by means of the twenty-seven divisions, how do they abide within the ungraspable center?
O Bhairava, by means of the sixfold differentiation of the movement through the channels,
the supreme Lord known as the individual soul (jīva) resides in every single wheel.
And for that which is called Cañcaki, how can there be liberation from bondage? Please explain the three trees, both externally and internally.
O Great God, what are the mudrās of Khecarī and the others? How may I truly understand the Samayamudrā of the Supreme Goddess?
What was previously called the "House," and how does it become the "Western"?
O Maheśvara, tell me this supreme secret distinction.
Whose stability should one understand, and whose dissolution is established?
O Supreme Lord, what is produced by the union of these two?
How do the six types exist through the differentiation of the letters of the *mātṛkā*?
Tell me, [how] the mandalas exist through the twenty-sevenfold division.
Tell me of the knowledge of time regarding the arising and setting [of the planets] in their respective positions, as well as deception through the application of contrary methods.
And how will liberation occur through this very body, given the threefold authority, the commitment, the convention, and the maṇḍala?
There is no alms-food to be found even in the three worlds;
all this, in brief, [is so]. O Bhairava, grant me your grace!
The illustrious Bhairava said:
I shall tell you [this], of which there is no doubt; it is secret, to be concealed, and well-guarded.
That primordial tradition of the Kula was formerly concealed by me.
The northern [face] is at the root of the southern, and the southern is at the root of the western;
the western is to be joined with the northern—thus is the Supreme Power (Parāśakti) established.
The second [face], named Bhairava, which was previously established on its left side,
is suspended above and hangs down from the left half of that [head].
One should first establish the root; then the two conch-like [channels], the left and the right;
and finally, one should employ the third by means of the left and the right.
That power which is supreme, most subtle, and established as half a syllable is joined at the end of that former jewel, turning to the right.
This indeed is a digit (kalā) of Bhairava, established as the Linga;
O Goddess, this is the power of Rudra, from which the moving and the unmoving have arisen.
In the center, through the yoga of churning, Bhairava together with the Śaktis arose,
O Supreme Goddess, in both unmanifest and manifest form.
From Ājñā, another non-attainment called Kukārā has emerged;
she is that very Śakti who stands below in manifest form.
Above that, in the form of the state of Nirvāṇa, Bhairava resides;
this body, consisting of six sheaths, is established as Kulakaula.
O lady of excellent hips, he becomes a Kula-yogin;
here, worship should be performed according to the sixfold Kula lineage.
In the region of Oṃkāra is Jāla, while Pūrṇapīṭha is situated to the south; to the left is Śrīkāmarūpaka at the front.
O Goddess, one should worship the letter *ra* and the letter *mi*, joined with the five *praṇavas*, situated in the middle and established within three *oṃ*s.
Endowed with the syllable Oṃ and encapsulated by the five Praṇavas,
it should be worshipped with effort upon the Jālandhara seats.
The Goddess, established at the beginning of the gods, [is the letter] *ca* and the letter *ṣa*;
situated in the center of Pūrṇapīṭha, she should be worshipped with great effort.
O Goddess, one should worship the letter *u* of the first [syllable] preceded by *siddhi*, and the letter *ca* on the seat in front, O Great Goddess, encased within the *praṇava*.
One should worship these four seats within the triangle of power;
as for the five jewels in the center, that which was previously mentioned by me in the ritual of placement (*nyāsa*).
Having first worshipped the letter *vi*,
then the letter *kā* which follows it, then the third letter *ma*, and the fourth letter *svā*.
One should worship that form, which resides in the five and is likewise the sixth,
situated in the midst of the powers of Rudra, by means of the yoga of emanation.
This pure group of six gnoses and the group of four—listen now to them:
Siddhanātha in the form [of Ā], and Svākāra as the second.
One should worship the third with the syllable *ca* and the fourth with the syllable *ma*;
these four, known as the Ādisiddhas, should be worshipped in the locations of the sacred seats (*pīṭha*).
Situated within the midst of the Five Goddesses and established upon the path of Kula:
the first goddess is in the letter *mā*, and the second is by means of the letter *sa*.
The third is with the letter *ū*, and the fourth is the one preceded by *ca*;
the fifth goddess, O lady of excellent complexion, is established in the letter *ku*.
O you of great majesty, perform the worship situated in the fifth syllable:
the letter *ā*, the letter *a*, and the third, the letter *u*.
In the place of Rudra’s crest, one should worship the triad;
then the tetrad, the pentad, the hexad, the tetrad, the pentad, and the triad.
O Goddess, this has been declared in six ways by means of convention;
its twenty-seven divisions exist both externally and internally.
O Goddess, those who have received the Kula initiation and consecration, and the Kula yogis, should know this;
above this, one should worship the lineage of gurus in their proper order.
In front of that, one should worship three of the family trees together.
When? At the left ear and likewise at the right ear.
The Kadamba is at the tip of the nose; these three trees have been thus described.
Ānanda (Bliss) ends with the Visarga, while the cavity (Vila) consists of the letters from Ka to Ṭha.

The Lord is to be known as beginning with *ḍa* and ending with *ha*; the Yogin begins with *la* and ends with *la*; likewise, the *tīta* [portion] begins with *ka* and ends with *kṣa*; and the syllable of the foot (*pāda*) is *smādakṣa*.
One should worship the sixfold [deities]: Ānanda, Bali, Prabhu, Yogin, Atīta, and Pāda.
Prabhālokā, Lalitā, Utpalā, Pratimā, Śaṅkhā,
Siṃdyā, Śivā, Manmathā, Sadyā, Puruṣā, Śāntī (Martyā), and Bhairavā.
Raktā, Sarvapuṣpā, Kamalā, Khakhā, Gāgā, Gaṇā,
Aghorā, Eka-caryā, Saṃpūrṇā, Sūryā, Khaḍgā, Devā, Aśvā, and Candrā.
Pūrṇā, Ḍamarukā, Vinayā, Ātmā, Tatvā, Sthavirā, Dhanuṣā;
Pādā, Pavanā, Śabdā, Brahmā, Bhāvā, Yogā, Svagā, Raktā.
Teja, Ātmanā, Utpalā, Bhuvana, Kula, and Saṃkṣepa Piśāca—
these are the sixfold names of the Siddhas.
Through the conjunction of the letters of the Mātṛkā, one should cause the primordial [syllables] to arise;
having extracted the initial phoneme, it is established in bliss at the end.
One should worship with diligence according to the distinction of six locations;
one should worship at the location of the throat through the sixteen pure divisions.
The letters from 'a' to the final 'visarga' should be worshipped with diligence;
whichever letter of a name occurs first, situated in the middle of this [sequence].
O fair-faced one, he shall indeed become that very Kaulika;
they are accomplished through the yoga of meditation alone—of this there is no doubt.
Furthermore, one should know that the twelve-spoked Anāhata [cakra] is in the center of the heart,
while the [thunderbolt] weapon arises in the middle of the throat.
Through the application of names, syllables, and so forth, the yogi undoubtedly attains accomplishment;
there is no doubt in this for one who is always devoted to its placement (*nyāsa*).
O Goddess, the Svādhiṣṭhāna, which consists of six parts, is situated in the middle of the navel and located between the thighs; it is pierced by ten jewels.
One should know that which is situated between the *valas* (enclosures) and worship it in the place of the *liṅga*;
O Goddess, that which is situated between the *valas* is established in the letters within the *ādhāra*.
O Goddess, one should worship with effort the four Siddhas there;
furthermore, in the place of the Command (ājñā), between the eyebrows, are two syllables.
O Goddess, one should worship two Siddhas who bestow the accomplishment of the Command (ājñāsiddhi),
which is established prior to the names of the letters of whichever Cakra [is being practiced].
Previously, its name was proclaimed through the yoga of bliss;
whatever is one's own station, family, and wheel exists according to the distinction of names.
Through the accomplishment of his application of meditation, there is no doubt in this matter,
as long as the knowledge of his own family name has not been realized by those who contemplate the families.
In that vision, there are no external objects of worship, nor indeed any worshippers;
having diligently worshipped the wheel situated within the perfectly completed maṇḍala.
I shall now fully explain that according to the ritual procedure for the mandala,
using saffron, sandalwood, or indeed red lac or honey.
Ghee, milk, water, honey, or the juice of lac;
likewise, gorocanā, camphor, or even the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
One should prepare the mark with vermilion ground with water, or else with beautiful ashes; for Viṣṇus, one should use cow dung, or whatever is available.
On a seat made of precious gems, arising from the splendor of the sun and moon,
on a crystal, on a king’s turban, or on a most beautiful seat— what [is the difference]?
Whether made of gold produced from a single horn, or silver,
or on a copper pedestal, or on a base of śrīkhaṇḍa sandalwood;
Either on a seat of red sandalwood, or one made from Aśoka or Madhūka wood,
or on a cloth placed upon a stone, or on a seat of clay, or even upon the bare ground.
A maṇḍala measuring one cubit (pāṇi) should be made in the center of the four seats;
it should be fashioned with the left hand and provided with three girdles (mekhalā).
Therein, O Dear One, one should fashion a beautiful six-spoked wheel situated in the center,
endowed with the qualities of Śiva and Śakti, exactly as previously described by me.
Therein, in the center, the six spokes and the four seats of the Siddhas (siddhapīṭha) should be diligently worshipped according to their twenty-seven divisions.
With *jātī* flowers, *kadaṃba*, *pārijātaka*, and *pāṭala*; with *kunda* and *bilva* leaves, as well as *maruka*, *vīra*, and *yūthikā*.
Mallikā flowers, red lotuses, jasmine, blue water-lilies,
fragrant blossoms, and saffron filaments.
The foremost of practitioners should perform worship according to their means,
offering incense, lamps, food offerings, and libations with wine.
One should offer the three types of *phalguṣa* offerings and then commence the recitation (*jāpa*).
The mantra of the Goddess consists of thirty-two syllables, encapsulated by five *praṇavas*.
Having performed the supreme binding of the mudrās— one thousand, five hundred, and even half of half of a hundred— he should prostrate and make his offering.
One should perform the salutation with one limb, five limbs, eight limbs, or indeed all of them; then prepare the sacrificial porridge (caru) and the seat (āsana).

Having prostrated, one should diligently consume the *phalguṣa*, the illuminating food offering (*dīpa-naivedya*), and the *āsava* situated before [the deity], and then perform the ritual dismissal (*visarjana*).
O Goddess of the gods, this pure sixfold deposition (ṣoḍhānyāsa), together with its sequential order, has been explained as it has come down through the lineage of tradition.
Whoever performs this ritual placement (nyāsa) three times a day, by day and by night,
[frightens] ghosts, spirits, piśācas, yakṣas, kuṣmāṇḍas, and rākṣasas.
O beloved, those others who are harmful also behold the form of the Purifier through the yoga of constant practice within six months, O lady of excellent countenance.
It burns away all sins, including even the killing of a Brahmin;
furthermore, I shall again describe those other holy days of the Kula.
The sixth [tithi] in the month of Bhādrapada, the fourteenth of the dark fortnight of Āśvina,
the ninth of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, and the fourteenth of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa.
O Goddess, the full moon day of Pauṣa, the excellent fourth day of Māgha,
the ninth day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, and the thirteenth day of Caitra [are auspicious].
The third day of Vaiśākha, the bright tenth of Jyeṣṭha,
the eleventh of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, and the new moon of Śrāvaṇa.
The sixth [lunar day] in the forest (Āraṇya) is to be known as the fifth during the sun's southern course;
the Festival of Lamps and the scattering of dust should be performed during the sun's northern course.
These ancient [Parvas], O Goddess worshipped by heroes, have been recounted;
whoever should always worship this Parva with a pure inner self, [attains the highest goal].
O Goddess, she rejoices together with twelve Aḍas and the Khecaras.
Always perform the sequential worship according to this very procedure.
Furthermore, O Goddess, that which resides within the body must be worshipped with great effort;
when one is endowed with devotion, success is attained—of this there is no doubt.

The devoted gods, having attained the state of Sugata through the power of destiny and being liberated from merit and demerit, long for the worship of his feet as the cause for severing the cycle of existence.

I bow to that Ādinātha who has led [beings] to nirvāṇa, by whom the impurities of the moments were seized, who is consecrated by the moon and sun, and who has attained the stainless state; thus I perpetually pay homage to him. || 1 ||
That which is the perfected one, the primordial, saluted by the best of gods, and worshipped by yogis— that glorious Oḍḍiyāṇa is adorned with various multitudes of qualities and divine assemblies.
Having proclaimed this loudly in the abode of the best of gods amidst the assembly of yogis, I, having sought refuge through praise, bow eternally to his pair of feet in this manner. || 2 ||

By him [the Lord], the venerable seat named Jālandhara— which is pervaded by [him] and adorned with the peaks of the best of mountains and mountain caves— has been made a treasury of conquered qualities; it is the deity worshipped by the lord of yogins, who is himself a treasury of virtues.
Having gone to the base of the netherworld (pātāla), by whom various venomous serpents and demons were crushed—
bow down perpetually to that Śrī Khecakranātha for the sake of attaining the goal of the Lord of the Cakra (Cakrīśa).
With devotion, he placed his two feet [upon the ground]. || 3 ||
She who, by the name of Śrī, sports with the pleasures of desire like a doe in the realm of Śiva, having abandoned the Śrīpūrṇapīṭha which is adorned with divine throngs and many graceful steps.
Having consumed all lamps without remainder, I, having gone for refuge through praises to his pair of feet adorned with a multitude of divine qualities, thus bow eternally. || 4 ||
Having abandoned Śrī Kāmarūpa, while being entreated by the Yoginīs night after night in their abode,
he went to the divine seat of Kailāsa on the peak of the best of mountains, where he gratified Śambhu.
In that very moment, he returned once more to Laṅkā; there the glorious Mātali, Lord of Laṅkā, was consecrated as lord, his pair of feet worshipped by hosts of celestial maidens. || 5 ||

By him, many duties and offices were performed; by him, various people were crushed under the weight of his wisdom; by him, through manifold and intense methods, sentient beings were perfected and established in the abode of the supreme gods.

I perpetually prostrate to the fifth Lord of Conduct (Caryanātha), who has wandered through the fields, seats, and sub-seats having experienced enjoyments through intense ignorance, and who has performed the "thunderbolt-splitting" (*vajrasphoṭa*) [of the ego].
He who is named Vajra, who is devoted to the practice of the vow of awakening; by whom Rudra was propitiated after performing the vow of knowledge (*vidyā-vrata*);
and who, having assumed authority there in the abode of the best of gods by forming the *śakti-khaṭvāṅga* mudrā, was diligently consecrated as a deity by the preceptors of the best of gods.
May the Sixth Lord, the treasury of all virtues, protect me, the foremost among the masters of yoga. ||7||

Thus, she who is renowned in the lineage of the Siddhas as a treasury of all virtues on the path of Mantra; who is worshipped in heaven by Brahmā and the other gods, in the world of mortals by the lords of sages devoted to the Krama practice,
and in the netherworld and the atmosphere by all the various venomous serpents and divine beings residing therein.
I bow down to him who has reached the state of praise and conduct. || 8 ||

Whoever himself praises [the Goddess] three times with these eight verses, by the grace of the Goddess, the perfected Command (siddhājñā) shall proceed for him. The multitudes of obstacles perish, and the arising of the divine birth occurs.

The Bindu, residing upon the seat of Ananta within the heart-lotus, endowed with the three measures (mātrās), situated in the center of the orb of light, and adorned by a shimmering divine maiden— [meditate upon it].

I bow to that vast, eternal, and renowned syllable known as Oṃ, which is served by multitudes of various perfected beings (siddhas), which pervades the universe, and which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

The lamp of the flame of the fire of gnosis, which removes all impurities, is well-established in the center of the navel; it is encircled by the elephants of the directions and contains the abode of the three worlds, situated in the right, left, upper, and middle.
That place is the form of gnosis, where the Supreme Power (Parakalā), joined with the eye and the half-moon, delights.
Salutations to you, the divine seat (pīṭha) named Jālandhara, which consists of both uneven and even steps. || 2 ||
Abiding above the *svādhiṣṭhāna*, consisting of all qualities,
situated within the center of the *piṇḍa*, filling it completely,
resembling a shimmering lightning flash, he purifies that which is already perfectly pure.

Obeisance to you, the bulbous root (kanda) whose nature consists of the eight vowels, the world situated above it, the central knot that is split open, the triangular region therein, and the full seat (pīṭha) where the sun, moon, and fire reside. || 3 ||

Therein arose the aggregate of elements, the universe composed of all qualities, the sign of space characterized by the three gunas, which, following the curvature of the ages, descended like the movement of a water-wheel.

O you who are like a cruel jewel in the midst of Brahmā’s time, who have attained perfection through yoga, who are a perfected incarnation, who are bowed to by the three worlds, and who can assume any form at will—salutations to you (I bow to you). || 4 ||
O lady of excellent complexion, the four sūtras of the pīṭhas have been described;
they should be known, according to the divisions of the wheels, as residing within the body and bestowing perfect accomplishment.
Now I shall fully describe the nature of the Trikhaṇḍā;
she should be worshipped with diligence, for she bestows the fruit of all accomplishments.

Omniscient Narayana, you who have come to satisfy us, you are the one who is not subject to decay; you are the pervasive, the all-pervasive, the supreme light, the all-encompassing, the all-encompassing.

Phreṃ! To the King of the Nārīmaras, Phreṃ! To the one who has marked the purpose of the form of the essence, Phreṃ! To the one who is the seat of the power of the Nīmi-gāśakas, Phreṃ! To the one who releases the mind from the bonds, Phreṃ! To the one who is the womb of the lineage of the Yadrārus, Oṃ Phreṃ!
At the end of this vidyā and so forth, the end is established at the beginning;
it should be understood according to the division of the words in reverse order, as it occurs.
For one who has fallen away from the conduct of the samaya, when the transgression of violating a woman occurs—
whether through ignorance or delusion— this [practice] is the liberator from all sins.
And at the conclusion of the sequential worship (kramapūjā), the Supreme Goddess is to be recited.
Śrī Bhairava said: "Those men who mock those who cause the ruin of yoga..."
The circles of the yoginī commitments (samayacakras) that have been taught, as well as the observances of the vows (vratacaryās).
Those of evil conduct who always defile the Vīramelāpaka mantra spoken by Śiva and create obstacles for it.
I shall explain the sixfold suppression as it is extensively taught:
when the mother is in her fertile season, the wooden seed (dārubīja) is established within her.
O Goddess, having extracted the sixfold [mantra], make it joined with all the bindus;
one should also cause the first syllable to be conjoined with Ananta (the nasal ṃ).
O Goddess praised by heroes, the second [syllable] is joined with Mālinī and the tongue;
the third is situated at the end of Dhruva; and the fourth is with Bhūtīśa.
Having joined the fifth at the end of *khe* (or *kṣe*), and the sixth situated at the end of *loka*,
this jewel of a mantra, preceded by five *praṇavas*, originates from the head.
One should write the *praṇava* (oṃ) and the third [syllable] (*ma*) devoid of the *bindu*. These nine seed-syllables are situated thereafter in their pure form.
At its end, O Goddess, one should worship the mantra named Ḍākinī, ending with *svāhā*, consisting of twenty-three syllables.
One should know that the staff of the trident of Mālinī, situated in the [group of] nine as previously established,
is of six kinds, just as it was previously established.
Place the letter *ri* (which is *sa*) joined with a *bindu*, established with effort;
at the end is the second jewel (*ratna*), and before that is the seed-syllable of Lakṣmī.
Having recited the *anāhṛta* mantra, one should thereafter recite the *rākṣasī* mantra;
at its end, one should repeatedly say "dry up" (*śoṣaya*) in blood-red syllables.
O Goddess, one should employ the second [mantra] ending with "svāhā"; of this there is no doubt.
In the ninth and the third [sections], Pinākin Bhairava is established.
It is indeed divided into six parts according to the sequence as before;
by means of the union with the third jewel, each preceding part is joined with the one before it.
O Goddess, one should perform the extraction; at its end is Maṇipūraka.
At its conclusion, "Lākinīmāṃsa gṛhṇa gṛhṇa" is recited.
One should perform the worship ending with *svāhā*, knowing the Yoginī to be situated in the navel;
having extracted the syllable *saṃ* (the *saṃvaka*), [one should worship] in six ways as before.
O fair-faced one, at the end of the seventh [syllable], one should join it with the jewel [mantra] by means of the fourth;
then, one should again apply that same original seed-syllable at the end of the jewel.
At its tip is the self-consecration (svādhiṣṭhāna) conjoined with the names of the Śākinīs;
it is said to be in the form of the syllable "śam," and it utters "grahṇa-grahṇa" (seize, seize).
The mantra ending with "snānyu svāhā" should be diligently worshipped;
Mālinī, whose phonemes are proclaimed, resides on the peak or on the left arm.
One should know that it is sixfold, as previously established;
O Dear One, the eighth, the fifth jewel, and the ninth are as before.
Place the name of the *ādhārayakṣiṇī* at the end of that;
[insert] "jṛmbhaya" (make yawn), and let the syllables be situated in two places.
The worship of the fifth [deity] is performed with the yoga ending in *svasti* and *svāhā*;
having extracted Krodhabhairava, he resides at the beginning of the eleventh.
These six are likewise differentiated by the application of the vowels used previously;
with the *māyā* [syllable *hrīṃ*] joined at the end of the seed-syllables, the first seed-syllable is placed before them.
At the end of the *tapa* [mantra], one should extract the goddess Kākiṇī preceded by the command (*ājñā*).
At its conclusion are the two words "kravyamā" and "saṃhara."
The worship of the sixth [syllable] with *gudaṃ* at the end of the conjunction is called the "sixfold suppression," which effects the suppression of the three worlds in an instant.
Having accomplished it according to the prescribed rite— which produces immediate conviction—
one should perform the recitation for each individual mantra ten thousand times, O lady of excellent complexion.
And one should perform the fire sacrifice (homa) with a tenth part [of the materials] as prescribed for the collection of the yoga;
for the first [part], one should prepare the bark mixed with human ghee.

Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and likewise Rudra constitute the three qualities within the world;
this body is composed of three parts, established as three sections throughout one's lifespan.
The threefold Puruṣa separately enjoys the three portions of Time:
the portion of Brahmā, the portion of Viṣṇu, and the portion of Rudra.
Those thirty-three years are established as being divided into three parts;
the Lord of Creatures (Prajāpati) moves as the wind that has entered the cage of the elements.
As long as Brahmā remains embodied and experiences [time] in the form of Time (kāla),

When Brahmā sets and Hari rises,

Even by that yoga of Viṣṇu, there may be a deception of knowledge;
