Its number is likewise such, five times that immediately following;
it too is located in the Ocean of Milk and measures one hundred thousand verses.
O lady of excellent complexion, that which has been performed and recited according to the ritual procedure is accomplished;
it is shaped like a bow, circular in form, and originates from the *latājāti* species.
There is no doubt that for one who has accomplished the recitation of the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*), this [attainment] is reached through the power of that very mantra,
ending with the word "sma."
In heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld; among the fourfold collection of beings;
among the two-footed and the four-footed; and among those without feet and those crowded with many feet.
O beautiful one, authority has been granted by me to Kāmadeva;
he has entered all bodies and remains established in the form of creation.
I shall further proclaim the extraction (uddhāra) as it truly is;
listen with a one-pointed mind regarding that of Kāmadeva.
Having extracted the five *praṇavas* and so forth, one should place the second syllable of the wrathful deity below the letter *sa*, and provide its seat there.
Joined with *dhruva*, *mālā*, and so forth, Ambikā resides upon its head;
joined with *lokādi* at the beginning of the head, this is the second, most excellent seed-syllable.
O Goddess, one should provide for him a seat consisting of the letter *ju*, situated above the *na* in the ninth [group], and placed below it, with the *nāga* (the letter *ha*) in its center.
One should fashion [the deity] together with the three forms (trimūrti), seated upon a staff-throne;
they call the third seed-syllable that which is adorned with a bindu at its head.
Having extracted the letter beginning with *aṃ*, situated below the [letter] of Śiva (*ra*),
joined with Ananta (*ha*), and adorned with a bindu at its head.
Below Arghīśa, O Goddess of the Gods, is the seat consisting of the color of sinew joined with the upward-facing [syllable]; there, fashion Bhṛgu and Bhairava.
Mounted upon the power (śakti) Dīpinī and adorned with the letter at the end of Kṣe,
the fifth [vowel] conjoined with the bindu is the supreme means for attracting the life-force (jīva).
Furthermore, O Goddess, know that Bhṛgu-kaṃ is situated solely before that;
then make Śūla-daṇḍa and Snāyu-varṇāsana follow it.
Having extracted the seed-syllable of Devaśukra and pierced it with the subtle Rudra, one mounts it upon the staff of the trident; this is the eighth, most excellent seed-syllable.
Having extracted the letter ending in *ka* (k), adorned with the syllable of liberation (*kaivalya*),
mounted upon the first of the Mothers (*mātar*), this ninth [syllable] bestows creation.
Having collected the vomited [substance] from one who has vomited it into the abode of beings,
one should fashion the three forms together with the trident at their front.
Having placed Ananta in the east, one should draw Krodha at its end;
one should join the letter 'ka' ending with the red-colored head situated within the Krodha.
In front of that, you and the seed-syllable should be extracted at the end of the full moon;
one should place the five seed-syllables at the beginning of the vidyā and at the end in reverse order.
The thirty-two-syllable vidyā has arisen from the center of Meru;
this vidyā is supremely secret and is endowed with the five arrows.
Through his uncommon yoga, this one whose banner is the sea-monster (Makaradhvaja) has attained perfection;
so too have the Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Daityas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras.
O beloved, those humans, serpents, and whoever else there may be—
by means of the practice for accomplishing the *vidyā*, they are praised as being equal to Kāmadeva.
Whomever he touches with his hand, whomever he beholds with his eye—
through the contact and conversation, the world becomes overwhelmed.
O Goddess, whatever women there are in the three worlds melt at the mere sight of you;
O Beloved, it is the opinion of the sages that you would agitate them—of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess of the Gods, by the end of this worship, the three worlds shall come under one's control;
it is especially a great cause of delusion for women.
The arrow of ignorance remains fixed within his body for one who constantly recites this mantra one hundred and eight times.
Kāmadeva himself has directly taken recourse to a human body.
Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter in the *Pārameśvarīmata*, concerning the extraction of the mantra of Vajranityākāmadevī.
The Goddess said: "O Lord, regarding that which was previously mentioned by you— the womb-sacrifice (garbhayāga) which is so difficult to attain—
how can the birth of a son occur for women who are childless?"
Tell me that, O Mahādeva, for the benefit of human beings.
Śrī Bhairava said:
That which is the great secret Vidyā was accomplished by Kāmadeva.
By that very same application of ritual procedure, I shall now describe the sacrifice pertaining to the womb.
This creation, consisting of Brahman, has also arisen from the center of Mount Meru;
I shall fully describe that procedure exactly as it is.
In a well-purified area of ground, free from anthills and the like,
having entered the Brahmin soil, the practice should be white and yellow.
They say that the earth consisting solely of yellow color is for Kṣatriyas,
while the earth named Vasundharā, which is slightly reddish-yellow, belongs to Vaiśyas.
She who is red and black is proclaimed to be a Śūdrī;
indeed, for whichever caste [the practitioner belongs], he should have the womb-sacrifice (garbhayāga) performed by her.
Having taken land within its own respective portion, it shall become fruit-bearing;
however, on lands belonging to other castes or other portions, obstacles will arise.
O Goddess, if the ritual is performed by one who is not an Ācārya, it becomes fruitless;
therefore, one should examine the ground and always perform the sacrifice there.
On an auspicious spot of ground, having lifted up the earth with one's hand,
a hut should be diligently constructed using wood from trees that yield milky sap.
Adorned with beautiful mallets and graced by desired powders,
that site, measuring eight cubits in dimension, is most beautiful.
Having carefully constructed an altar made of milky wood,
one should prepare four white archways, each accompanied by a water-pot.
Having cleansed the altar with mango sprouts,
O beloved, one should prepare there a six-cornered mandala centered upon a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa).
In each corner, a water-pot together with a vardhanī vessel should be placed,
filled with the five jewels and endowed with pure [substances].
One should cause them to be filled with flowers, garments, unbroken grains, and lamps;
there should be auspicious songs and instrumental music, and the sound of the four Vedas.
Having taken fire from a hearth produced from milk-tree wood,
one should then cast that fuel arising therefrom into the center of the sacrificial pit.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
this "Ointment of the Immortals" was previously described by me through the division of Manthāna.
Having gathered the family materials, from them the production of the *piṇḍa* occurs;
it should be sixty *prasthas* in weight, free from defects, and perfectly pure.
O beautiful one, the Kulācārya should prepare the sacrificial oblation (caru) using a very splendid copper vessel combined with cow's milk.
Having sealed [the site] with the mudrā, one should offer the bali-oblation in the four directions:
earth, a water-pot, unbroken grains, lamps, as well as the sacrificial pit, the fire-drill, and the oblation material.
O Goddess of Gods, the five substances that have arisen from the five elements— namely the vessel, water, and so forth— the Root Vidyā, having been consecrated seven times, should employ them.
Having worshipped with diligence, prepare the sacrificial porridge (caru) placed within the fire;
O Goddess, as long as that is being accomplished, one should mentally recite the mantra.
One should diligently maintain a posture joined with the left [nostril] and observe silence;
by the grace of this mantra, success is attained—of this there is no doubt.
Having carefully caused [the seed] to descend until it becomes cool,
when the fertile period has arrived, on the fourth or fifth day;
Having performed the bath with fragrant and beautiful substances with great care,
one should sit upon a comfortable seat in the center of the fourfold pedestal.
One should perform prostrations and consume [the substance] with great care;
through the application of right conduct, a person certainly becomes one who has transcended worldly existence.
The left [hand] is declared to be female, while both together are neuter;
one should give with the right hand to all Brahmins and practitioners.
O Goddess, one should worship the teacher with jewels and gold, as well as among the wandering minstrels, young maidens, and others who bear the sectarian marks, and even the kings.
Having prostrated, one should offer the gift of a cow, the gift of land, and likewise the gift of food,
as well as divine ornaments and garments.
O Goddess, this Garbhayāga is established within the Kula path;
it must not be given to those among the world of the *paśus* who harbor hatred toward the Āgamas.
One should cause the consecrated initiate to receive the divine *caru* of the Kaula;
otherwise, there will be a loss of accomplishment (*siddhi*), of this there is no doubt.
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter in the Pārameśvarīmatigarbhayāga.
The Goddess said: "In the former Mṛgāvatāra, the ritual practice was performed by you."
The yoginīs produced within your body are of six kinds.
"O God of fierce splendor and great power, you who have been entreated by them for ten million and a quarter [years], grant me your own body."
By eating the ball offered by you, mixed with wine,
all those situated in the wheel attain satisfaction and sport.
O Lord, you have spoken again, saying "Seize! Seize!
and thus performed the protection of yourself in the midst of the vajra-circle.
I too have heard such news from within Kailāsa:
she has emerged from my body, born of great wrath.
Illuminating the entire world like twelve suns, I devour the supreme circle of Yoginīs; of this there is no doubt.
Then, O Mātali, the gods headed by Brahmā arrived before me;
I, who am protected by the assembly of yoginīs, was praised by them with various hymns.
Having understood the splendor, the seed-syllable, and the color,
you have manifested the one renowned as Trotalā, the tenth messenger, endowed with forbearance.
Its limbs are the wheels, and the seat together with the mudrā;
when properly joined, these perform the rites of both restraint and grace.
And seventy million verses were spoken by the one with the face of the past;
therein arose the supreme Tantra known as Totala.
Regarding that vidyā which resides there, measured at one hundred thousand feet:
what kind of power does it possess, and what are its ritual actions?
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"The great Tantra Trotala originated from my eastern face.
O Great Goddess, the Prajāpati Sūryavaṃśa attained perfection through this."
Even there, one who is terrified by fear should be sealed with three mantras—
at the beginning, middle, and end— by means of the phonemes, measures, and so forth.
Furthermore, what is the nature of its opening by means of the three mudrās? Three mudrās have been fully described as being situated within Meru.
It is obtained only through the successive lineage from the mouth of the Guru;
for knowledge devoid of this transmission can never be perfected.
It creates great obstacles and brings about the destruction of children, wife, and wealth;
it also causes disease, the torment of grief, and various kinds of suffering.
Therefore, with every effort, perform the correct opening;
once the Great Knowledge is opened, that life shall become fruitful.
It is accomplished; there is no doubt in this, for it bestows the fruits of the four castes (or four classes).
O Goddess, listen to how she becomes situated within the center of Meru.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
the Kulācārya must fashion a pill possessing auspicious characteristics.
Furthermore, one should empower her again with the root-mantra twenty times,
beginning from the feet up to the head, over all those locations where the mantra resides.
The practitioner should apply the *tilaka* according to the sequential method;
it is declared to be a great protection throughout the three worlds, including all things mobile and immobile.
The Nāgas, Vidyādharas, and others do not create obstacles at all;
thereafter, one should assume a seat in the form of a lion with a distorted face.
I shall explain its extraction as it exists in the center of Meru;
they know the Rudra Saṃvartaka to be situated in the eastern half-face of Śiva.
The seed-syllable of the five-faced one, joined with Krūrānanda,
and preceded by Saṃvarttaka, shall be the second syllable.
Furthermore, O Goddess, the third syllable of that [mantra] should be in the east;
taking the one situated in the middle of the left, there is Bhairava, the sinew, in the ninth.
The fourth is declared to be Jayantī, situated in front;
the fifth is the supreme seed-syllable of him whose seat is the serpent.
Having taken the one situated in the middle of Rudra, adorned with the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti),
one should always write the seventh [syllable], the goddess Ambikā, at its end.
Having extracted the syllable beginning with *ṛ*, which is situated on the seat starting with *dhruva*,
and again, O Goddess, the serpent (*bhujaṅga*) situated on the seat ending with *ja*.
Furthermore, one should join these two syllables at the beginning;
the syllable arising from Krodharudra is situated in the middle, [marked by] *kṣe*.
One should fashion [the image] adorned with the three forms; O Great Goddess, make it joined with the Origin of the Worlds (Lokādi) and the twelfth seed-syllable of the Five-faced One.
One should grasp the fixed point situated in the middle of the bamboo tube which stands below;
it is renowned as being of universal color, and at its end (or within it) is that which resides in the middle of the hair.
One should indeed draw this pair of letters again in front of it;
then, O Goddess, [one should place] that which is situated in the middle, located below the letter *khī* (or *khā*).
Having extracted only the seventeen-syllable seed-mantra,
Mālinī and Vāyuvegā are situated on the peak of the left lord.
A serpent should undoubtedly be placed upon his head;
furthermore, these two seed-syllables (bījas) should be placed before him.
Having extracted the *praṇava* (oṃ) together with the *antaḥpraṇava* (namaḥ), and having placed [the syllable] standing before it at its end,
O Goddess, one should again append the end (*huṃ*) along with the *ananta* (phaṭ).
The seat is declared to be of cruel appearance;
it is fully described as having five faces, being a fierce seed-syllable of great power.
O Goddess of the gods, by the recitation of this Dharma-nārasiṃha mantra consisting of twenty-three syllables, that which occurs through one hundred thousand recitations [is attained].
Whatever herds of elephants there may be, overwhelmed by intoxication in their three states, they become free from pride at the mere falling of his glance.
By its scent, lions, tigers, elephants, spirits, ghosts, and rākṣasas meet their destruction or flee in the ten directions.
Neither lightning nor the clashing of thunderbolts, nor those minor rites,
nor poisonous machines, nor any great obstacles whatsoever have power over him.
When the *āsana* is perfected, great protection arises;
without the *āsana*, O Goddess, one is overwhelmed by great obstacles.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain what the root-mantra (mūlavidyā) is like,
how it is entirely free from obstacles, and what the nature of that living being (sa-jīva) should be.
Having extracted the syllable of the vital breath (praṇava), conjoined it with Sūkṣmarudra;
then, having surmounted Lokādi with the Śiras [mantra], make it conjoined with Trimūrti.
Again, having extracted that same syllable and placed it at the end of the *dhruva*,
with *nāda* and *bindu* added to the head, this is the second, most excellent seed-syllable (*bīja*).
Bhārabhūti, holding [the manuscript] below while Śikhara stands above,
together with Jhaṇṭīśena, [revealed] the supreme syllable of the Goddess’s mouth.
The goddess, situated in the midst of the mind, having grasped the supreme abode of Kūrma and Rudra,
is declared to be the seed-syllable of Rudra located in the throat of Tvarita.

Having grasped that which is situated in the middle of the lion and located below Dhruva, the power of knowledge (and action) is bestowed upon the head; the seed-syllable residing in the heart is established within the power.
Having extracted Saṃvartaka and joined it with Sūkṣmarudra, one should know this to be the navel-syllable of Trotala; of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess, once again, take that which is situated in the eastern part, having the color of Bhṛgu;
place it upon the seat in the middle of the serpent, and make it differentiated by the vowels beginning with *ḷ*.
With the vowel *ḷ* preceding it, and with the head (*śiraḥ*) given, situated upon the staff of the trident (*śūladaṇḍāsana*),
this is declared to be the seed-syllable (*bīja*) of Viṣṇu, which is the secret of Tvarita.
Furthermore, the goddess Mālinī, who performs the withdrawal, resides in the circle of the navel;
she is conjoined with the power of knowledge (jñānaśakti), and her seed-syllable of Brahmā is exceedingly difficult to attain.
O Goddess of beautiful countenance, it is situated upon the two thighs of Trotala;
it stands preceded by the nine letters beginning with *A* and ending with *R*, and is positioned above the end of *Prāṇa*.
One should know the seed-syllable of the Sun (raṃ) as being pierced at its head by a bindu, situated upon the seat of Arghīśa, and established between the two jātu-s, O Goddess.
The phoneme established as Bhūtādi is in the left foot, and Mālinī is not [there].
But further ahead of that, O Goddess, is the phoneme of Someśvara.
O Goddess, this Vidyā, which ascends through the sections beginning with Dhruva and includes the feet of Tvaritā, has been fully described; it is exceedingly difficult to attain.
And it has been fully explained that [all] are accomplished; there is no doubt in this matter.
The Goddess said:
"O Lord, previously you stated that [the lineage] remains sealed and hidden."
Therefore, O Protector, I know what they are like there.
The illustrious Bhairava said: That very Prajāpati, having become a Siddha through the power of this ignorance, also took up the *Trotalottara* at the eastern face.
Having quickly extracted the Vidyā, it is sealed with three mudrās;
the Sun is rendered devoid of splendor, and the Bird is deprived of its measures.
O Goddess of the gods, the seat is likewise devoid of the color of the head and is sealed with these same mudrās; for it too, such [a procedure] has been performed.
Each seed-syllable and the power of the five-faced one (Śiva) have been offered;
at the beginning, middle, and end, it has been rendered devoid of the three letters.
Sealed, they are initially devoid of color, yet they bestow the fruits of their own respective colors;
such is their opening, situated in the center of Meru.
For this [deity] as well, the nine (or ten) messengers are established beginning with Vajratuṇḍā;
all of them are endowed with the colors of the vidyās and so forth.

The ancillaries of knowledge, the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa), the recitation of mantras (jāpya), and likewise the fire sacrifice (homa)—when accompanied by the opening [of the door], the Goddess is accomplished; there is no doubt in this matter.
Within the previously mentioned mantra, however, is that which bestows the fruits of action:
namely, paralyzing, pinning down, and the breaking of enemy kingdoms.
The accomplishment of the Vetāla, as well as Piśācas, Rākṣasas, and others;
the emergence of a maiden from a jar, and the raining of clouds out of season.
Among them, there are the daughters of the Daityas and Vidyādharas, as well as the adornment [of these maidens],
the sword-garland, the collyrium, the trident, and the means for entering the subterranean openings (vivaras).
Pills, magical sandals, and the power of entering another's body; the nāgas, the nāga maidens, and whatever substances are made of flowers.

They are accomplished; there is no doubt in this matter. This is the supreme method for performing all types of summoning, as well as the sādhana of the yakṣiṇīs and the attainment of the power of moving through the sky—of this there is no doubt.
The ritual for the lord of the earth, the supreme invisible state (marked by a seal),
the forehead mark, the foot-ointment, and the assembly of the Yoginīs.
He shall undoubtedly become a universal monarch (cakravartin) among the Vidyādharas;
he in whose body Tvaritā resides shall possess incomparable good fortune.
She who, especially a queen’s wife, worships this [goddess] with the fivefold offerings accompanied by pure devotion;
A woman shall become the most excellent among a hundred thousand women;
even a man shall obtain a kingdom through worship—of this there is no doubt.
O beloved, this knowledge has been declared by me together with its key;
through the grace of this knowledge, it accomplishes all desired aims.
By means of one million recitations and a perfected fire-offering,
through the grace of this vidyā, one shall become a lord of the vidyādharas.
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, titled "The Extraction of the Entire Tvaritā," according to the Pārameśvara-mata.
The Goddess said:
"You previously promised the supreme Aghora mantra;
in what place did it originate, and of what nature is its power?"
The illustrious Bhairava said:
I shall tell you, without doubt, that which was asked by you—
the Aghora mantra, consisting of thirty-two syllables, known by its name.
In the *Rurubheda*, the *Mahātantra*, the *Siddhayogeśvarīmata*,
the *Svacchandalalita*, the *Ghora*, the *Mārttaṇḍa*, and the *Śivasādhana*.
In the *Trikhaṇḍa*, the *Niśācāra*, the *Yoginījālasaṃvara*,
the *Pracaṇḍapañcamuṇḍamālā*, the *Matsyodarī*, and the *Mahārṇava*.
In all these tantras, it is revealed as being devoid of life-force (jīva);
it is liberated from power (śakti) and vital breath (prāṇa), and is bereft of the five seed-syllables.
A mantra devoid of efficacy is never successful.
The Goddess said:
When a mantra is not successful, no conviction whatsoever arises.
What is the purpose of causing confusion among the gods, dānavas, and siddhas?
The illustrious Bhairava said: "By the grace of Aghora, I shall declare that supreme teaching which destroys all delusion, [and by which] the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas [were overcome]."
Through recitation and divine oblations, those Daityas of great power attained perfection;
bearing divine weapons, they were established in celestial vehicles.
All the deities, beginning with Indra, have been rendered powerless;
neither in heaven, nor on earth, nor in the netherworld is a rival to be seen.
And all that [purpose] has been secured by me through the mantra fastened with the pegs of the syllables;
the five seed-syllables have been formed, and it is filled with the letter *bha*.
The thirty-two-syllable mantra, devoid of seed-syllables, has been revealed;
it is the mantra accompanied by the syllable *bha*, with "namaste" situated in its center.
"Due to the eight stakes (kīla), this [mantra] of yours will not succeed at all.
The Goddess said:
"The Aghora is a great mantra that bestows all accomplishments (siddhi)."
"O Lord of Gods, grant me your grace, O Master, if you are pleased with me."
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"Excellent, excellent, O highly wise one, you who are compassionate toward practitioners!
I shall tell you, without hesitation, that which has been concealed by me, O beloved."
On a level plot of ground, free from depressions and elevations,
enriched with the beauty of scattered flowers, and perfumed with incense, fragrant substances, and the like.
In that auspicious and beautiful place, one should place a water-filled jar,
filled with the five gems and accompanied by lamps and unbroken grains of rice.
Having fashioned this [mandala] with its four directions smeared with white sandalwood paste and draped with white cloth, one should draw Mount Meru in the center.
Having worshipped according to the prescribed rite with the fivefold offerings and liquor in the company of Phalguna, one should extract the supreme mantra.
First, one should visualize Śrīkaṇṭha seated upon the peak of Kailāsa;
then, in front of him, one should extract the second seed-syllable from the Viśvamālā.
One should draw the bracelet of Śiva produced from his right arm,
joined with the Sadyojāta [face] and situated at the beginning of the letter 'A'.
The third [syllable] is Śūladaṇḍa, situated at the beginning of the group of nine;
joined with Jhaṇṭīśena, it is the third, most excellent seed-syllable.
Having extracted the syllable *bhūtīśa* (Bhū) and joined it with *akrūra* (Kṣ),
by the power of that seed-syllable, the Grandfather [Brahmā] assumed the form of creation.
One should know that the fifth [syllable] situated in the eighth (or seventh) position within this garland of planets is Mālinī, which arises from the seat.
The syllable ending in *ṛ* (ṛm) should be given to him, and a bracelet should be placed before him;
a serpent joined with the Sadyojāta mantra should be positioned in front of him.
To the east of the *ṛ* is the seventh, supreme seed-syllable, with its head broken;
having extracted the seed-syllable of Ambikā, it is situated upon the seat beginning with *na*.

One should know the seed-syllable of Viṣṇu to be that which begins with *loka*, is surmounted by the head (*śiras*), and has the three forms (*trimūrti*) pierced through it; it is the illuminator of all accomplishments.
After this, one should cause him to receive his second mantra, the serpent,
and both of these seed-syllables (bījas) before him.
Having extracted the Bhāgavamedhya [mantra], one should place the excellent Rudra-mantra of Āṣāḍhī,
joined with the Ṛṣi-pūrva, at the beginning, situated in front.
Having extracted the letter *ṇa* (which is the first letter of the word *sohya*), that which is situated at the end of *va*—
this is called the *saṃvarka*, known as Rudra, and it is situated within the bone.

One should offer the seat beginning with *na*; it is pierced by the power of the tongue (*jihvā-śakti*) and split at the head by the sprout (*aṅkura*). This is proclaimed as the seed-syllable of Lakṣmī.
By means of its recitation and fire-oblation, misfortune does not remain;
one should know it as the power of will, and one shall obtain the desired fruit.
Again, having extracted the *saṃvarta* [mantra], it is placed on the fourth seat of the sages;
they call the third which is established there "Mālinī-netra."
And the sixteenth is declared to be the Eye originating from Kūrma;
and the fourth in the eleventh [chapter] is Rudra originating from Śukra.
One should know the name Bhṛgu and write it at the end of the sixteen;
[one should write] the fourth among the elements and Rudra, who is born from the back.
The month of Āṣāḍha is preceded by the head of the letter *na*;
joined with the end of *ṛ*, that which follows it shall be *saṃvaka*.
One should know that it consists of twenty syllables; one should write it again at the end with the mantra (or tantra), and then write the letter born of Bhṛgu before it once more.
They know the supreme syllable to be conjoined with Jhaṇṭīśa;
having written Mālinī as the left limb, that which begins with Bhūta is established.
One should know Rudra, who is borne by the peacock, as originating from the belly;
he is mounted upon the seat of the trident-staff and is situated at the head of the letters beginning with *ṛ*.
The supreme heart-mantra of Cāmuṇḍā is conjoined with the syllable *Aṃ*;
that seed-syllable is most terrible, possessing a radiance like the fire of the end of time.
By the mere remembrance of this, Brahmā trembles.
Having extracted Raktabhairava from the western [position] of Atithi,
one should place Dhātrīśa upon his head and Rudra in front of him.
He too should again draw one mounted upon Raktā and colored red;
they know that which stands upon the seat up to the end of Dhruva to be the twenty-seventh.
The syllable *lohita*, which is situated as the ninth in the Rudramālā and is conjoined with Jhaṇṭīśa, is the supreme heart of Mālinī.
The fourth [vowel] in the eleventh [consonant], situated on the root-staff seat (mūladaṇḍāsana),
peaceful and placed upon the head, should be bestowed as it is distinguished by the grace of Rudra.
The seed-syllable, both supreme and inferior, is pervaded by the head [of the mantra] which is cruel;
merely by its utterance, [it effects liberation] throughout the three times, day and night.
The sin committed over twenty lifetimes is reduced to ashes at that very moment;
the seventh [syllable] is in the Rudra-mālā, while Mālinī is situated upon the head.
One should know that the *Kevalanta* consists of twenty syllables;
the third is the *Ṛṣimālā*, which they know as the *Nitaṃvamālinī*.
Rudra, born from the heart, is Mahākāla, the imperishable;
and in the eleventh [position] is the fourth, Bhairava, born from Śukra.
One should place Jhaṇṭīśa, mounted upon the seat in the midst of the nāgas, upon the head;
this supreme secret mantra consists of thirty-two syllables.
And Aghora is fully described as that which brings about the presence of supernatural powers;
whatever mantras exist in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld, they are all of divine form.
O Sovereign of the Asuras, these very [mountains] belong to the seven crores;
this great mountain with four peaks is seen at his side.
Thereafter, he is not thought to give even the extraction of the King of Mantras;
rather, he [rules] the earth as far as the ocean, filled with jewels and treasures.
One should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the guru; by bowing, one becomes free from debt.
Nevertheless, the worship of the guru must be performed with effort, accompanied by restrained conduct.
Having prostrated, one should offer the gift of a cow, the gift of land, and likewise the gift of food,
as well as divine ornaments and garments.
Having worshipped with diligence, he then requests the command;
O Goddess of gods, having obtained the command, he considers his body to have achieved its purpose.
Having received the instruction from the guru, one should then begin the sacrifice after diligently purifying the ground so that it is endowed with all auspicious characteristics.
One should establish a hermitage there and perform the consecration of the site;
first, a wooden stake shaped like a horse's hoof should be driven in, measuring one cubit in dimension.
Having recited the mantra of the messenger (dūtī) one hundred and eight times,
the practitioner should bury it in the middle of the ground, and then [bury] Agnidūtī above that.
According to that same procedure, he [should plant] a stake made of khadira wood;
likewise, devadāru to the south and vibhītaka to the southwest.
One should place that which originates from the Udumbara tree in the southwest,
that which originates from the Śiṃśapā tree in the northwest, that which originates from the Vaṭa tree in the north, and that which originates from the Bilva tree in the northeast.
The practitioner, intent upon the mantra, should perform the great worship;
he is a hero wearing the five mudrās and likewise clad in red and black garments.
One should sit upon a lion-skin seat, or in its absence, upon a deer-skin;
one should perform the ash-bath (bhasmasnāna), and thereafter the mantra-bath.
Having prepared sacrificial threads made of darbha grass, cotton, or hair,
the practitioner should perform the ritual placement on the limbs (aṅganyāsa) using the root mantra.
Purification of the hands occurs with a single recitation; the two hands are rubbed against each other. With one recitation at the heart, the head is formed by that same one.
They say the *śikhā* consists of one [syllable], one is situated in the *kavaca*, the *trinetra* is one [syllable] to be uttered; thus the mantra is established in six parts.
O Dear One, one should perform the ritual placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*) together with the *jāti* and *paṅga* mantras;
O Great Goddess, it should be worshipped as previously heard from the mouth of the Guru.
Saffron, sandalwood, gorocana, and honey—
these substances, together with blood, [should be used].
One should construct a square mandala and draw a lotus in its center;
at the beginning of the mantra, there should be syllables of the Vedas together with the letter 'a'.
At the end of the triad, at the end of the triad, and again at the end of the triad,
one should repeatedly utter [the name] by means of the differentiation of the mantra-seed through interlacing (vidarbha).
"O messenger accompanied by Brahmā and Indra, descend, descend! Homage!
By this rite, O Goddess, one should worship in the eastern direction.
Furthermore, the four syllables are interwoven with the *ka*-group:
"Māheśvarī, Agnidūtī, descend, descend, obeisance."
One should worship in the south-eastern direction.
The syllables "ghore ghore" are interlaced with the [seed] syllable according to the group.
[The mantra is: "Kaumārī, Yamadūtī, descend, descend, obeisance!"
One should worship in the southern direction.
Furthermore, the four syllables interlaced with the *ṭa*-group [of consonants] are:
Vaiṣṇavī, Rākṣī, Dūtī, Avatara-avatara, Namaḥ.
One should worship in the south-western direction.
In the fifth [syllable], the letters of the fourth class are interspersed with the *tavarga* [consonants]:
Vārāhī, Vāruṇī, Dūtī, avatara avatara, namaḥ.
One should worship in the western direction.
Furthermore, the four syllables are interlaced with the *pavarga* [consonants]:
"Aindrī, Vāyudūtī, descend, descend, namaḥ."
One should worship in the northwestern direction.
In the seventh [verse], the fourth letters of each group are interlaced with the *ya*-group:
"Caṇḍikā yakṣadūtī ca avatara avatara namaḥ."
One should worship in the northern direction.
At the end, the four letters [of the mantra] are interlaced (vidarbhitāḥ) with the *savarga* [syllable].
And in the northeast, [one should invoke]: "O Mahālakṣmī, descend, descend! Homage!
One should worship in the northeastern direction.
In the center, however, one should worship the supreme deity consisting of thirty-two syllables.
Then, having worshipped the lineage of gurus, one should worship Kṣetrapāla above them.
Then, having fully prepared the flowers, incense, food offerings, liquor, and fruit,
seal everything with the mudrā.
Padmamudrā, Karālī, Bhairavī, and Vikṛtānanā—
one should perform the binding of the mudrās and thereafter commence the recitation.
O beloved, O Maheśvarī, I shall fully declare that ritual procedure which has been kept secret by me;
she who is the Great Illusion (Mahāmāyā), the Power known as Kuṇḍalī.
One should contemplate that place of this mantra as having become one;
reciting it in its proper sequence, it is like the twelve suns.
Illuminating with its own splendor from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head,
it abides in the heart by way of piercing through the navel.
Furthermore, by means of the path of Viṣṇu and according to the sequence of the divisions of Rudra,
one should repeatedly effect dissolution into the station of the seat of Maheśa (the Lord).
In this very manner, having uttered [the mantra] according to the prescribed rule,
one should then utter it again in reverse order and cause it to enter.
By that very same application of the path, make it together with its own place;
O Goddess, this single utterance has thus been revealed as ninefold.
Whether it be crystal, pearl, or gemstone, the putrajīvaka,
that which originates from the great conch, or even that produced from rudrākṣa;
One should fashion the rosary so that it is held upon the ring finger;
one should move it along the path of Meru so that it does not touch the ground.
At the conclusion of the recitation, having consumed the sacrificial porridge (caruka) that was placed before the mantra,
the remainder should be given to those bound by the pledges (samayins), or else offered into the fires.
A celibate student, having conquered anger, avoiding contact with animals,
should eat at the end of the day, sleep on the ground, and keep his senses subdued.
One should commence the recitation of the mantra ten hundred thousand times and likewise perform the fire oblation (*homa*).
O Dear One, [one should draw] a beautiful hexagon arising from Śiva and Śakti.
One should also fashion the face with a measurement of one cubit;
then, taking the fire residing in the kindling wood produced from *bhūtadāru*.
In its center is the mantra of Aghora, who possesses a terrible form;
it is of a great, dark (or white) color, and as formidable as the palate and the netherworld.
One should contemplate the three eyes as being produced from the moon, the sun, and fire;
and one should again visualize the fangs as having the form of the fifth moon, as they are described.
One should visualize [the deity] with a large tongue licking [everything], with its face turned upwards;
one should then visualize the oblation entering into the middle of it.
And Mudrā Mṛgamukhī herself has been taken by him;
the oblations must be offered with a single utterance, entering into the mouth of Bhairava.
Then, with a steady inner self, one should perform the fire-oblation (homa) with a tenth part [of the total recitation];
thereafter, one should recognize success and employ it in all ritual actions.
One should draw a single mantra of four syllables separately upon each petal of an auspicious eight-petalled lotus.
They should be diligently established within the domain of the Lord by Indra and the others;
indeed, one should paint those very [deities] belonging to whichever respective class [is concerned].
As before, first taking [the first] from the north, the second from the east;
the third in the south-eastern quarter, and two from the west of Varuṇa.
O Rākṣasa, previously within me was that six-syllabled mantra,
joined with the wood of the Śiṃśapā tree and situated in the midst of human flesh.
One should offer oblations mixed with ghee one thousand and eight times;
then, without a doubt, a celestial chariot rises from the midst of the fire.
Mounted thereon, the great hero wanders through the fourteen worlds,
as far as the seven cosmic eggs; of this there is no doubt.
The messenger who is in the eastern direction, joined with sixteen syllables,
should offer oblations of *brahma*-flowers while being united with the mouth of Brahmā.
Perform the extraction ending with *svāhā*, and grant me the Brahmāstra,
which possesses the brilliant splendor of a blazing fire, [recited] one thousand and eight times.
It should arise within the center of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) and rest in the hand of the practitioner;
[therein reside] all the deities beginning with Brahmā and the fourteen worlds.
There is no doubt that this mantra, which is very difficult to conquer, slays [the enemy];
it is the nine-syllabled Māheśī residing in the direction of fire (the southeast).
Taking a *lāṅgalī* flower combined with the blood of a ram, one should recite the *pāvakāstra* mantra and say: "Give! Give! (*dehi dehi*).
It is accomplished with one thousand and eight [recitations]; of this there is no doubt.
Its splendor is equal to the fire of cosmic destruction (Kālānala) and is unbearable for all the gods.
The practitioner, when enraged, could burn the fourteen worlds;
she who resides in the southern quarter is known by the name Kaumārī.
By means of the application of saffron mixed with buffalo blood,
one should perform one thousand and eight oblations in the center of the sacrificial pit.
At the end of the *svāhā*, having uttered "O Six-faced One, give me power!
Give me power!", she rises—there is no doubt; this unfailing power is difficult to conquer.
If the great hero is angry with someone, he would kill him; of this there is no doubt.
[One should use] the leaves of the *vibhītaka* tree combined with the blood of an owl and a leech.
O Goddess, by means of the Vaiṣṇavī-dūtī-yoga and by performing a thousand oblations,
the exceedingly rare Candrahāsa [sword] is beheld at the conclusion of the fire-sacrifice.
While he holds the sword, no rival wrestler is seen;
[he should offer] one thousand and eight fuel-sticks made from the Varuṇa tree.
One should recite the Vārāhī mantra conjoined with fish-oil;
at the end of "svāhā," one should first say: "Grant me the Varuṇa-weapon."
O Goddess, if the practitioner so desires, he may grasp even that [object] within the vessel with his hand; then a great rain shall arise.
Furthermore, in the northwestern direction, she who is known by the name Indrāṇī [is worshipped];
through the oblation of *vajrī* leaves mixed with milk, [one attains her favor].
And by performing one thousand and eight oblations ending with "svāhā," the hero obtains the vajra through the power of this goddess.
If enraged, one would swiftly slay even one who were equal to Śakra;
and in the north, the goddess Caṇḍikā is established with eight syllables.
Having taken banyan leaves combined with dog's blood,
by reciting [the mantra] one thousand and eight times, the perfection of the mace will be achieved.
One obtains infinite wealth from a treasure-store within a vessel; one should know that to be inexhaustible. Now listen to what occurs in the northeast.
The practitioner, with a steady inner mind, should take one thousand and eight wood-apple fruits and offer them as oblations mixed with clarified butter.
At the conclusion of the fire sacrifice, O Goddess, the trident invincible even to the gods is seen;
it will slay [the enemy], there is no doubt, even if it were Brahmā himself or Hari.
When one performs the offering with the previous messenger using the reverse application,
[one should offer] that which is produced from *devadāru* wood combined with the blood of a horse.
The best of practitioners, having recited "Give me a chariot" at the end of the mantra, should perform fourteen thousand oblations in accordance with the prescribed ritual.
Without a doubt, O beloved, the great chariot-warrior Nandighoṣa is rising,
equipped with white horses, yoked to white [steeds], and adorned with banners.
Having mounted it, the Great Hero will undoubtedly fly up;
invincible to all the worlds, he is the destroyer, the creator, and the self-sovereign Lord.
By means of the yoga of inverted recitation, the lord of practitioners performs eight thousand oblations of *guggulu* mixed with clarified butter.
O fair-faced one, there is no doubt that he obtains a cloth produced from fire;
furthermore, O lady of excellent countenance, by means of this mantra, the opposite result is not obtained.
When the Yamadūtī has been accomplished through oblations by Gopāla, one obtains invisibility and a staff; of this there is no doubt.
And by reciting the Vaiṣṇavī mantra in reverse order eighteen thousand times with human flesh mixed with ghee, one shall attain the ritual procedure of the Rākṣasī.
The lord of practitioners undoubtedly creates forms that are the nature of illusory manifestation;
she is the messenger who exists through the reverse yoga and the Western [tradition].
O fair-faced one, by performing a thousand oblations of fish meat, one should know that all things are attracted; there is no doubt in this matter.
In the quarter of Vāyu, one should offer oblations of deer meat mixed with cow’s milk to Indrāṇī, one thousand and one hundred times.
One should know that he attains the perfection of the pill; there is no doubt in this matter.
When the messenger (dūtī) of one who is in the northern direction speaks in reverse order, [he succeeds].
One should offer *vaṭa* leaves combined with cow-ghee (*gavājya*, i.e., the essence of cows);
he obtains inexhaustible wealth—this was spoken by Īśāna.
By offering one thousand and eight oblations of *bilva* leaves combined with clarified butter to Mahālakṣmī in reverse order, one shall attain the siddhi of heroic rasa.
O Supreme Goddess, this rite of Aghora has been declared;
if one so desires, one may accomplish every rite through the power of this mantra.
Even if Mount Meru should move from its place, or the ocean should dry up,
or the sun should fall to the earth— I would rather swear these things to be false.

"Truth, truth, O Great Goddess, I have spoken this which is not false"—this is an additional reading found in another manuscript. This portion was extracted from an ancient palm-leaf manuscript by copying it letter by letter. The subsequent portion, up to the end of the fifty-sixth chapter, was written by one who resided in Madhyadeśa in the year 1488 Śaka.
In some places, it is seen as "in the Pārameśvara system" or "in the Kubjikāmata system.
Thus ends the fortieth chapter, named the Aghora-nirṇaya, in the eighty-four thousand [verse] Navakoṭi-saṃhitā of the Pārameśvara system.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
"O Blessed One, everything situated within Meru has been fully explained."
The extraction of all vidyās according to the different movements within the channels (nāḍīs).
O sinless one, you previously taught the Vajraprastārikā vidyā and likewise the Brahmavidyā, distinguished by thirty-two syllables.
That knowledge which has been taken up as worship in many ways within the Tantras and the Kula lineage—
by the mere extraction of its vow, one is liberated from sins.
By means of the sequence of extraction (*uddhāra*), and by the sequence of worship and meditation, [one attains the goal];
yet how can anyone [attain it] through the number of syllables, the vow (*vrata*), the fire-oblation (*homa*), or the libation (*tarpaṇa*)?

What kind of ritual placement (nyāsa) should one perform, or how should the means of accomplishment (sādhana) be? What indeed is the requisite substance, and who specifically is the qualified practitioner?
O Lord of Gods, that which was employed by you in a most secret manner,
and all that was perceived by the lords of the gods, has been related in brief.
O Lord of the Gods, if you have supreme compassion for me and if my love is most excellent,
then tell me this here in the midst of Mount Meru.
Īśvara said:
O Goddess, although this has not been told to anyone and must likewise be kept secret,
I shall nevertheless tell you of that knowledge which is a means for attaining wealth through its power.
O Goddess, in the city of Viṣṇanātha, the Grandfather of the worlds was propitiated by Śakra for the sake of victory over the lord of the Daityas, and he was pleased.
O Goddess, O beautiful one, although I know the Vidyā in its various divisions, O Great Goddess, you ask me again and again.
Nevertheless, I shall speak; now, pay close attention.
In a very level (and secluded) place, with incense, lamps, perfumes, and musical instruments...
When the accumulations have been gathered, one who conducts himself with accumulated virtue and is free from the view of sacrificial animals,
having received initiation from a guru himself, [should practice] by a river, on a mountain, or in a cave.
Having remained thus, one should perform the placement (nyāsa), as well as the placement of mantras;
for the liberated soul should extract the single sequence situated in the center.
O Goddess of the Suras, one should know that the thirty-two-syllabled deity, consisting of both cause and effect, is the eternal first letter located at the navel.
In the middle of the left side, within the belly, resides Nivṛtti among the Kṣatriyas;
through its union with the letter *ḷ* and so forth, it is the second supreme seed-syllable.
In the eleventh Ṛṣisthāna, Ambikā is established within the vital breath;
furthermore, Akrūra, bestowed by Śiva, is situated in the midst of the Sādhis.
O Goddess, the fourth letter, which is the best among those situated within the vowels (eḷa),
is located in the middle of its own portion, where you are established in its lap.

Then, for the sake of purifying the heart, one should place the sixth seed-syllable, Sureśvara, in the temple of Rudra within Naraka, according to the conjunction of the letters beginning with Dhruva.
In hell, [place] the first letter; make Mohinī adorned.
Lambodarī is in the white house, and Sāmānī is on Gandhamādana.

One should recognize the "color of the mother" (mātṛvarṇa) among those in whose midst the Guru resides; O Goddess of the Gods, it is subtle, situated in the center of the syllable *kāra*, and pierced by Bhairava.
One should know the tenth mantra as being joined with the time (kāla) in the middle of the cough (kāsa);
in the eleventh position, that of the seer (ṛṣi), it is pierced by Jhaṇṭīsena.
O Goddess, the thirteenth seed-syllable of Māyā consists of twelve syllables;
by placing Kālāmoḍī within it, it likewise becomes Ambikā.
O Goddess of the gods, in the center of the *kāra* is Jhaṃṭīsenā;
Vajriṇī is situated below Ambikā, and Ananta is on Gandhamādana.
O Goddess, that which is situated in the middle of the watch (yāma) is declared to be the eighteenth;
having grasped the center of the Dhenu [mudrā], it is joined with the subtle on Mount Mandara.
The great Rudra named Kāla is situated there in the center;
he is joined with Sūkṣma at Mandara, the eleventh station of the sages.
One should understand the twenty-first, or one should begin the lowest [scale] as the twenty-second;
however, the twenty-third syllable is exclusively the middle of the gamut.
O Goddess, situated between the two *palas* in the abode of Rudra, O auspicious one, there is a twenty-four-syllable mantra; from that, the state of Rudra arises.
The Bhūtādi [mantra], situated in the blood and established at the top of the head, is conjoined with Bindu and Bhairava; it possesses the brilliance of the fire of time (kālānala).
O Goddess, listen now to that which consists of twenty-eight syllables, following this: "He He Ta," with the letter *tha* situated upon the staff of the trident.
The great Rudra named Kūrma is adorned by Sadyojātanātha;
I am the pure middle [face], remembered as Vadhātrīśa Bhairava.
One should place the subtle Bhairava named Pālīśa in the middle of the *yāma*,
and the eight [deities] trampled by Ananta in the middle of the *yuga*.
With *aṃ* situated in the middle of *ambikā-jīva*, ending with *kṣe* and adorned by *svarga*,
the thirty-two-syllable deity is thus established through these phonemes.
O Goddess, in heaven, on earth, and likewise in the netherworld, the abode of the serpents,
there are Nārada, Aṅgiras, Bharadvāja, and Gautama.
Viśvāmitra, Vasiṣṭha, and others, as well as other gods and dānavas,
and even the planets such as the moon and the sun, [are all subject] to the power of this vidyā.
O Goddess, those who abide in the worlds and move about day and night—
even Makaradhvaja, O Queen of the Gods, having propitiated the Supreme Lord— [attain their goals].

O you who are endowed with all auspiciousness, the best of gods [should be worshipped] by means of the application of the six-limbed nyāsa and by the sequence of the placement of the syllables (varṇanyāsa).
For one who is pure in soul, the vehicle [of liberation] arises; that occurs through the practice of *nyāsa* and other such rites.
O lady of excellent complexion, the *nyāsa* must be learned directly from the mouth of the Guru.
By the grace of the Guru’s command, success is attained; there is no doubt in this matter.
Having performed the ritual placement (vinyāsa) again according to the rules, one should meditate upon and contemplate the form.
One should meditate upon her who possesses the luster of the color of kunda flowers and vermilion, the bestower of the sovereignty of speech,
who holds a single bow and arrow, a noose, a goad, and displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
Likewise, she holds a citron in her [upper] right hand and a full skull-cup in her left;
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva [are her attendants].
O Dear One, those resembling yellow, reddish, dark blue,
and white collyrium should be placed at the four gates, two each, starting with Hetuka and the others.
The individual (āṇava), the empowered (śākta), and the divine (śāmbhava)— by means of these, or by all of them together,
[one attains] the state of the initiate (samayin), the seeker (sādhaka), and the master (ācārya), through initiation performed for the sake of liberation.
The Śāmbhavī Vidyā is composed of consciousness and is the power (śakti) consisting of the three qualities (guṇas).
Here, the initiation according to the human method taught by the Guru consists of many kinds of rites.
O Goddess of the gods, one should offer the *arghya* to the deity invoked in the mandala;
one should offer it with milk to the Brahmins, and likewise with clarified butter (*ājya*) to the kings who rule the earth.
The Vaiśyas [should worship] with honey, and the Śūdras with sugarcane juice and *āsava*;
thus the primary daily worship shall be performed, as well as that which occurs on every festival day.
Alternatively, the monthly worship ought not to suffer interruption;
that which arises from honey is the cause, and it is proclaimed as *āsava*.

Having obtained the four substances with the four [offerings] beginning with ādhaka, there is an abundance of fruit for those seeking liberation; from worship, however, there is only a very slight subsistence.
The worship of the Vṛtti yields greater fruit for one who desires [liberation];
O Parameśvarī, worship accompanied by all the Vṛttis is the highest.
Thus is this great mantra, which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation upon men.
Now, I shall further explain another [mantra] that is relevant to this context.
"Id vā ruktaṃ ga mo maṃ kha mu khyalajasya sa vi de dhi ra va da vi da dhe he ma vi da dhe | O Goddess of the gods, the syllable beginning with 'dhru' (dha), then two in the middle of the portion,
conjoined with Sūkṣmabhairava, shall become [the mantra] * * * * saṃ."
In the Navarudramālā, [the mantra] is established upon the seat beginning with Dhruva;
in the group of nine, the initial syllable is indeed conjoined with the seat beginning with Dhruva.
The great Rudra named Śveta [is there], and Māyādevī is present by her own nature.
The ninth [seed-syllable] is remembered as that which is pierced by Jhaṃṭīśa, the subtle Vāruṇa [syllable] differentiated [by it],
and Krodhīśa joined with the power (śakti) of the ankle (gulpha).
O Goddess, the seed-syllable named Sadhāsa is situated in the middle of the sword;
it is split in the midst of the water, red, and subtly divided.
The great goddess Lambodarī is adorned with secret power (guhyaśakti);
if there is the sound "yadi" when afflicted by the sun (ravārta), the name Vaktra follows immediately thereafter.
Furthermore, O Goddess, having assumed the color of wrath and being seated upon a seat of speed,
one should visualize Mahākāla alone and Vaka as the eighteenth.
Again, O Great Goddess Śivā, having extracted the letter Krodha (K), joined with Indu (I) and born from Bindu (M), I blew another [conch] adorned with Akrūra (R).
The letter situated in the middle of the portion is indeed the solitary one, repeated again and again;
it is the letter Bhṛgubhairava, the twenty-second—of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess, Vajriṇī is situated in the midst of water;
in Śiva, Dīpanī is joined with it, its head pierced by the Bindu.
O Goddess, the portion belonging to Varuṇa shall indeed become pure once again;
he is the Great Rudra named Kāla, tall in stature and adorned with ornaments.
In the middle of the Guru, and likewise again in the middle of Yāma,
it is joined with the wife of Fire (svāhā) and adorned with thirty-two syllables.
This very Vidyā, the supreme kalpa that bestows the fruits of all desires,
was formerly realized by the Buddha as the enchantress of the three worlds.
The one who bears the banner of Rudra conquered the lord of the Daityas named Tāraka;
O Goddess of Devas, he attains success by reciting it one hundred thousand times—of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess of the Gods, through the offerings of oblations kindled in the Brahma-cave, and by the increasing of milk, clarified butter, and honey,
you have attained all desires in all your wishes.

Having thus performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-vinyāsa*) for the Lord of Men, who is like Indra, [the practitioner] should worship with laughter, break the path on the vehicle, and [offer] the breath of destruction; he is the one who has attained all auspiciousness for the sake of the auspicious, the one who is free from impurity like Mālinī, and who possesses the matted locks and earrings.
One hundred thousand [times] from one's own perspective.
When the oblation is made with *bilva* flowers, *arka* fuel-sticks, and *arka* fruits, he bestows wealth;
he stands upon a white lotus leaf, adorned with necklaces, bracelets, armlets, and earrings.
I shall describe Padmanābha, who is red in complexion, smiles, has tawny eyes, three faces, and three feet; he holds a lotus, a water-pot, a cup, and that [specific] day.
Having fashioned that maṇḍala, and having adorned it with the finest garments and ornaments,
[one should offer it] to Pūrvabhadrāya, Pūrṇabhadrāya, and Vanamālin.
O lords of men, one should worship Yaśarendra,
who possesses six hoods and is joined by Mātṛbhairava, the bestower of prosperity.
This single mantra alone, through the differentiation of qualities such as time and so forth,
brings about both prosperity and misfortune for oneself and for others.
Possessing various forms and powers, what could they not accomplish for those who understand them?
They can even dry up the oceans and shatter the cosmic egg.
They cause the worlds to lose their luster as they withdraw everything;
they may render the eloquent mute, and they may make even the Lord of Speech himself silent.
They can make a poor man a giver of wealth and deprive a lord of riches of his fortune;
they can instantly make one long-lived and cause one whose life has ended to continue living.
They can turn a woman into a eunuch in an instant and even release one who is bound;
this occurs according to the number of mantra-syllables available and their respective capacities.
The deity is indeed the power of the mantra whose body and limbs are fully perfected;
for it is thus that the form of the divine body consists of mantra.
Because it protects the one who recites it, it is therefore known as a mantra;
it is imperishable because its nature is not subject to decay, and it is fruitless [in the sense of worldly results] because it is partless.
He makes the gods joyful, causing the faces of the inhabitants of Tripura to melt away,
by deluding that one who is intent on casting his net of illusions.
O Supreme Goddess, in this tantra she is called Tanamudrā;
she who has no son, no disciple, and who is devoted to gods, Brahmins, and gurus.

If it were given, there would be a loss of spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*) and the deity would descend upon you as a calamity. Thus, for the sake of your household, this has been revealed to you today.
"O Goddess, what else do you ask? Tell me all that.
The Śrī Devī said:

The practitioner should meditate upon [the body] as divided at the feet and joined with incense, lamps, and so forth;
